May 17, 1939.
8039A(1)
MEMORANDUM ON THE LOCAL PIG TRADE

Local situation prior to the recent establish-
ment of the "Shanghai Livestock Market"

Sometime following the outbreak of local hostilities
the areas adjacent to the International Settlement and
the French Concession in which the majority of the local
pig hongs were located, were rendered inaccessible to
local pig traders and in consequence the latter had had
some, though not serious difficulty in securing fresh
stock for the local market. With the withdrawal of the
Chinese forces from the Shanghai area and the subsequent
general improvement in the local situation, a continuous
supply of pigs from Kiangsu was maintained without inter-
ruption. The usual source of supply of pigs for local
consumption has been the northern and western parts of
the Yangtze Delta at which places the local pig hongs
have stationed brokers as their agents for the purpose of
making purchases of stock and arranging their trans-
portation down river. Throughout the ensuing period
of approximately one year and up to the Spring of 1939,
the demand for pork in the foreign controlled areas was
met in a satisfactory manner by local merchants engaged
in this field of trade, while the price of pork was
maintained at a reasonable level. In the early
part of April, 1939, the pig hong owners and the various
steamship companies alike began to experience difficulties
in the business of transporting pigs from Singkeng, a
small river port in Kiangsu. The Japanese authorities
in this area commenced control of the transportation of
pages.zh:
1939年5月17日。
8039A(1)
关于本地生猪贸易的备忘录

近期“上海牲畜市场”成立前的本地局势

在当地战事爆发后的一段时间内，国际租界和法租界附近的大部分本地猪行所在区域变得无法进入，导致本地猪商在获取供应本地市场的新鲜货源方面遇到了一些困难，尽管并不严重。随着中国军队撤出上海地区以及随后本地局势的普遍改善，来自江苏的生猪连续供应得以维持，未曾中断。本地消费生猪的通常来源是长江三角洲的北部和西部地区，当地猪行在这些地方派驻经纪人作为代理，负责采购货源并安排沿江向下运输。在随后大约一年直至1939年春季期间，外国控制区域对猪肉的需求得到了从事该贸易领域的本地商人的满意满足，同时猪肉价格维持在合理水平。1939年4月初，猪行老板和各轮船公司开始在从江苏一个小河港兴庚（Singkeng，音译）运输生猪的业务中遇到困难。该地区的日本当局开始控制运输

pages.en:
(2)

pigs and compelled the pig brokers to pay a tax of
$2.00 per head on pigs intended for transportation
to Shanghai. Foreign-owned steamships loading
pigs were also interfered with and were either obliged to
unload their cargo at Singkeng or, upon reaching
their destination, obliged to pay an additional charge
of $2.00 on every pig on board. The Japanese
authorities, in enforcing these measures, were reported
to have only one object in view, namely the prevention
of the loading of pigs on foreign vessels but they
could be loaded on Japanese vessels.

At the beginning of the current year, it was
reported that a movement was afoot in Hongkew to
establish a pork monopoly in the Northern and Eastern
Areas of the International Settlement, sponsored by three
Chinese, who were obliged to solicit the aid of a
Japanese in order to conform with the requirements of the
Japanese Authorities which prohibit the establishment
of purely Chinese concerns in Japanese controlled
territory. The following persons were concerned in the
attempt:-

1. T. Moriyasu,
Lane 1034, House 28, Point Road. Tel. No. 50829.
2. Kee Tsong-hwa (顧托華), proprietor of the Yu Kiang
Pork Shop, 11 Seymour Road, near the Market, and
the Heng Dah Pork Shop, 258 Rue de Wei-hwei.
3. Fong Han-yuen (馮孝元), owner of a meat stall at
Ward Road Market.
4. Kiang Ah Pao (江阿寶), residing in an upstairs room
of a cake shop on Medhurst Road near Connaught Road.
5. Lee Sin (羅森), who acted as an interpreter.
pages.zh:
(2)

猪只，并迫使猪经纪对拟运往上海的每头猪缴纳 2.00 美元的税款。装载猪只的外资轮船也受到干扰，要么被迫在兴庚（Singkeng，音译）卸货，要么在抵达目的地时，被迫为船上每头猪额外支付 2.00 美元的费用。据报道，日本当局在执行这些措施时，只有一个目的，即禁止将猪只装载到外国船只上，但允许装载到日本船只上。

今年年初，据报道虹口地区有人企图在国际租界北部和东部地区建立猪肉垄断组织，由三名华人发起，为了符合日本当局禁止在日控领土内设立纯华商号的规定，他们不得不寻求一名日本人的帮助。参与此次企图的人员如下：-

1. T. Moriyasu，
Point Road（音译）1034 弄 28 号。电话 50829。
2. 顾托华（Kee Tsong-hwa），裕江肉店店主，地址在市场附近的西摩路 11 号，以及恒达肉店，地址在维岳路（Rue de Wei-hwei，音译）258 号。
3. 冯孝元（Fong Han-yuen），华德路市场肉类摊位业主。
4. 江阿宝（Kiang Ah Pao），居住在康纳路附近麦赫斯特路一家糕点店的楼上房间。
5. 罗森（Lee Sin），担任翻译。

pages.en:
(3)
The people mentioned above are known to have secured
the premises No. 19-21 Miller Road (Hongkew District)
where, on January 1st, 1939, an attempt was made to
establish a monopoly under the title of the Young Foong
Company ( ). The attempt proved a complete
failure and on January 6, 1939, the premises were closed
and the project was completely abandoned. Enquiries
so far reveal there is no connection between the defunct
Young Foong Company and the present "Shanghai Livestock
Market."

The formation of the "Shanghai
Livestock Market."

Owing to lack of necessary data concerning the
establishment of this organ, the exact date of the
formation of the "Shanghai Livestock Market" cannot be
ascertained with any degree of accuracy and it is held
probable that it came into existence without formal
procedure. This "Market" first attracted the attention
of the Municipal Police on April 10, 1939, when a branch
office was established in Room 127, Embankment Building,
400 North Soochow Road.

On April 12, two notices were published in the
"Eastern Times," one of which stated that the market
would commence functioning on April 15, at the temporary
address of Sze Yechow Road, and that a permanent market
was being built at the corner of Chaoufoong and Yuh Hwa
Roads (O.O.L.). The other notice stated that as from
April 15, 1939, the market would be the sole agency
for the transportation and sale of all kinds of livestock
and instructed pig dealers, livestock brokers and
boatmen engaged in the transportation of livestock to
register with the market between April 16 and 30.

Enquiries made at the branch office of this "Shanghai
Livestock Market" in the Embankment Building show that
it is promoted and operated by a Japanese named Matsuhara
pages.zh:
(3)
上述人员已知已租下米勒路 19-21 号（虹口区）的房产，并于 1939 年 1 月 1 日试图以“永丰公司”（Young Foong Company）的名义建立垄断。该尝试彻底失败，1939 年 1 月 6 日，该处所关闭，项目被完全放弃。目前的调查显示，已倒闭的永丰公司与当前的“上海牲畜市场”之间没有任何联系。

“上海牲畜市场”的成立。

由于缺乏关于该机构成立的必要数据，无法准确确定“上海牲畜市场”的确切成立日期，据信其成立未经过正式程序。该“市场”首次引起工部局警务处注意是在 1939 年 4 月 10 日，当时其在北苏州路 400 号堤岸大厦 127 室设立了一个办事处。

4 月 12 日，《字林西报》（Eastern Times）刊登了两则公告，其中一则声明市场将于 4 月 15 日开始运作，临时地址位于四州路（Sze Yechow Road，音译），并在朝丰路（Chaoufoong，音译）与玉华路（Yuh Hwa Roads，音译）拐角处（O.O.L.）建设永久性市场。另一则公告声明，自 1939 年 4 月 15 日起，该市场将成为所有种类牲畜运输和销售的唯一代理机构，并指示猪商、牲畜经纪和从事牲畜运输的船夫在 4 月 16 日至 30 日期间向市场注册。

对在堤岸大厦设立的“上海牲畜市场”办事处的查询显示，该市场由一名名为松原（Matsuhara，原文此处有汉字“松井”，但拼音对应 Matsuhara，依指令保留原文并注）的日本人推动和运营，

pages.en:
(4)
松井 ) with a Chinese named Wang Te-Jang (王志强),
noting as the answer, who claim to have secured the
necessary permission from the Japanese Military
authorities and the "Reformed Government.
With regard to the address at 5 Yochow Road,
enquiries show that prior to the local hostilities
this site was occupied by the Ning Po Dr. Hsia
(夏施泰兴) Slaughter House and recently by the Chang
Chun (長順) Trading Company which deals in pigs.
The Head Office is at 514 Ningpo Road and is operated
by a number of Formosans namely Messrs. Chow Ih-yau
(周錫堯) and Ling Hwei-nan (林輝南) and a number of
Chinese including Mr. Yang Fu-zung (楊輔臣), owner of
the Fuh Loong (復隆) Pig Kong, Li Vee Hou Li, Rue
Lafayette. These individuals when sounded denied
knowledge of the new Livestock Market. In this
connection, lengthy enquiries were conducted at the
branch office in the Embankment Building and information
was obtained that negotiations were then still in
progress between the market authorities and the Japanese
Military Police for the transfer of the lease of 5
Yochow Road to the Market.
A visit has been made to the site of the proposed
permanent market at the corner of Chaoufeon Road and
Yuh Hua Road but no sign of construction work was
observed.

Object of the "Shanghai Livestock
Market."

In forming the "Shanghai Livestock Market," the
Japanese and Chinese authorities behind the project
are understood to have cherished the hope of eventually
effecting a monopoly in the Shanghai pig trade. Their
pages.zh:
(4)
松井 ) 以及一名名为王志强（Wang Te-Jang）的华人，据称他们已从日本军事当局和“维新政府”获得必要的许可。
关于耀州路（Yochow Road，音译）5 号的地址，查询显示，在当地战事爆发前，该址由宁波夏施泰兴（Dr. Hsia (夏施泰兴)）屠宰场占用，近期则由经营猪只生意的长顺（Chang Chun）贸易公司占用。总办事处位于宁波路 514 号，由数名台湾人经营，即周锡尧（Chow Ih-yau）和林辉南（Ling Hwei-nan）先生，以及数名华人，包括复隆（Fuh Loong）猪行老板杨辅臣（Yang Fu-zung）先生，地址在霞飞路（Rue Lafayette）。当被试探询问时，这些人否认知晓新的牲畜市场。就此事宜，在堤岸大厦的办事处进行了长时间的查询，并获得信息称，市场当局与日本宪兵队之间仍在就耀州路 5 号租赁权转让给市场一事进行谈判。
有人曾前往朝丰路（Chaoufeon Road，音译）与玉华路拐角处的拟建永久市场遗址查看，但未观察到任何施工迹象。

“上海牲畜市场”的目的。

在组建“上海牲畜市场”时，该项目背后的日本和华人当局据理解怀有最终实现上海猪肉贸易垄断的希望。他们的

pages.en:
( 5 )
suggested measures for the registration of pig brokers,
dealers and boatmen at the Registration Office at its
branch office in Room No. 127, Embankment Building, 400
North Soochow Road, between April 18 and 30 and later
extended to May 31, 1939, can only be assumed to be a
preliminary step towards the enforcement of a monopoly
which, it is said, will be effected from June 1, 1939.

Reaction of those affected
by the new project

When it became publicly known that a Japanese
sponsored "Shanghai Livestock Market" was in the course
of formation in the early part of April, 1939, apprehen-
sion was apparent among the local pig traders who could
foresee the trade being adversely affected and all
sorts of impositions being imposed.

Before dealing with the steps taken by the local
pig dealers in opposition to the measures of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" directed at the collection
of a levy on pigs, it is proposed to review briefly
the present situation in the local pig trade as follows:-

There are two markets: one, the so-called Northern
District (Settlement) Market located at 275 Penang Road,
and the other, the so-called Southern District (French
Concession) Market located at 311 Rue Pere Fross. These
two markets have a joint delivery office in Room 286,
264 Kiangsu Road and have control of 83 pig houses.

The Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Fang, Nantao, closed
on the outbreak of hostilities. The pig dealers
belonging this guild, are, however, maintaining without
much publicity, a "Southern & Northern District Pig
Hong Traders' Joint Office" in the residence of a
lawyer named Chang Yih ( 張翼 ) Liang Jing Tsung,
Rue Lafayette. Mr. Chang was secretary to the now
defunct Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Fang, Nantao, and
pages.zh:
( 5 )
建议措施要求猪经纪、经销商和船夫于 1939 年 4 月 18 日至 30 日（后延长至 5 月 31 日）在北苏州路 400 号堤岸大厦 127 室的分支办事处登记处进行注册，这只能被视为实施垄断的初步步骤，据说该垄断将从 1939 年 6 月 1 日起生效。

受新项目影响者的反应

当 1939 年 4 月上旬公众得知一个由日本人赞助的“上海牲畜市场”正在组建中时，当地猪商中明显表现出担忧，他们预见到贸易将受到不利影响，并将面临各种苛捐杂税。

在讨论当地猪商为反对“上海牲畜市场”征收猪只税款而采取的步骤之前，拟简要回顾当地猪肉贸易的现状如下：-

有两个市场：一个是所谓的北区（租界）市场，位于槟榔路 275 号；另一个是所谓的南区（法租界）市场，位于神父路（Rue Pere Fross，音译）311 号。这两个市场在江苏路 264 号 286 室设有联合交货办事处，并控制着 83 家猪行。

南市四方街的猪行公所在战事爆发时关闭。然而，属于该公所的猪商们在不太公开的情况下，维持着一个“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”，地点在霞飞路良静宗（Liang Jing Tsung，音译）律师张翼（Chang Yih）的住所内。张先生曾是已倒闭的南市四方街猪行公所的秘书，也是

pages.en:
(6)
a staff employee of the now defunct Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Shanghai City Government.
It should be mentioned that the person Wong Ts-jen,
who assists Mr. Matsuhara in the management of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" as related above, was also
a secretary in the employ of the now defunct Pig Hong
Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao.
As the first step towards the controlling of the
livestock trade, the authorities of the "Shanghai
Livestock Market" in the middle of April, 1939, proceeded
with their plan of enforcing a tax of $2.00 per head on
pigs transported to Shanghai from Fompo which method was
assisted by the Japanese authorities who posted men at
Singkong, Northern Kiangsu, for the purpose of seizing
the pigs in enforcing the tax of $2.00.
On April 13, 1939, a number of local pig hongs held
a meeting in the "Southern & Northern District Pig Hong
Traders' Joint Office," 1 Liang Jing Wang, Rue Lafayette,
to consider counter-measures to be taken against the
enforcement of the new levy by the "Shanghai Livestock
Market." Mr. Hung Fen-kiang(洪文江), Assistant
Manager of the Northern District (Settlement) Pig Market
at 273 Penang Road, who presided, made an announcement
that out of a total of 53 pig hongs, 47 had pledged to
refuse to join the "Rogue Livestock Market." According
to the pledge, in order to fulfil the duties of a Chinese
citizen, the person pledging his word is bound to refuse
to cooperate with the "rogue" establishment and is
willing to submit himself to any punishment should he be
found to have broken his pledge. After discussion,
the following resolutions were reached:-
pages.zh:
(6)
已倒闭的上海市政府社会局的一名职员。
值得一提的是，如上所述协助松原先生管理“上海牲畜市场”的王志仁（Wong Ts-jen，音译）先生，也曾是已倒闭的南市四方街猪行公所的秘书。
作为控制牲畜贸易的第一步，“上海牲畜市场”当局于 1939 年 4 月中旬着手执行其计划，对从枫泾（Fompo，音译）运往上海的每头猪征收 2.00 美元的税款，该方法得到了日本当局的协助，日本当局在江苏北部的兴庚（Singkong，音译）部署人员，目的是通过扣押猪只来强制执行 2.00 美元的税款。
1939 年 4 月 13 日，多家当地猪行在霞飞路良静王（Liang Jing Wang，音译）1 号的“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”举行会议，商讨对抗“上海牲畜市场”强制征收新税款的对策。主持会议的是槟榔路 273 号北区（租界）猪市场副经理洪文江（Hung Fen-kiang）先生，他宣布在总共 53 家猪行中，有 47 家已承诺拒绝加入“流氓牲畜市场”。根据承诺，为了履行中国公民的职责，做出承诺的人必须拒绝与“流氓”机构合作，并愿意在违背承诺时接受任何惩罚。经讨论，达成以下决议：-

pages.en:
(7)
1) That a committee of seven persons including Mr. Sun,
Yen-king and Mr. Chang Yih be formed to take safe
custody of the pledges.
2) That a manifesto containing the decision of the pig
hongs to refuse to join the "Livestock Market" be
published in the Chinese press.
(3) That should the "Livestock Market" insist on a
monopoly, all of the 47 pig houses who had pledged
their word should suspend business rather than submit.
Following this meeting, a circular was issued on
April 23, 1939, in the name of the old pig hong guild by
the "Southern & Northern District Pig Hong Traders' Joint
Office mentioned above, to local pig houses, urging them
to insist on non-cooperation with the "Shanghai Livestock
Market."
On April 18, 1939, in pursuance of one of the
resolutions adopted at the above meeting, the pig traders
inserted a notice in the Chinese press reaffirming their
attitude and urging members to stand against cooperation
with any "illegal organizations."
Towards the end of April and in the early part
of May, 1939, cases continued to come to light in which
various consignments of pigs arriving from Tampo were
intercepted on the Whangpoo and later unloaded and detained
in Hongkew by persons claiming to be officials of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market." Negotiations were once
stated to have taken place between the Nisshin Kisen
Kaisha, which was responsible for the transportation
of some of these consignments, and the individual pig
hongs to which the pigs were said to belong, but no
tangible results are known to have been achieved and
a shortage of pork ensued.
In view of the repeated interference with the
arrival of pigs from Tampo by the Japanese-sponsored
"Shanghai Livestock Market," a number of local pig

dealers held a meeting in the Southern District Pig
Market on May .., at which counter-measures were discussed
and the following decisions were adopted at this meeting:-
(1) That pig dealers should persist in their opposition
to the collection of taxes and that they should
sacrifice their business rather than attempt a
compromise under threats.
(2) That in future, the pig hong owners shall jointly
share the losses sustained by any of their members
as the result of interference in the transportation
of pigs. Those who secretly compromise should be
severely punished.
(3) That the pig hongs would cease to transport pigs
from Kompe should there be made to control the
pig trade by compulsory means.
(4) That letters in the name of the Pig Hong Guild be
sent to the Shanghai Municipal Council and the
C.M.P., and the Ratepayers' Associations to request
assistance.
Under these circumstances, the local pig hong
owners despatched telegrams to their brokers and agencies
in Northern Kiangsu advising them to cease the
transportation of pigs pending a final settlement of
the present controversy. In consequence arrivals of
pigs have been greatly curtailed and this has in turn
caused the price of pork to rise to $1.00 per catty,
which amounts to an increase of about 40 per cent
compared with the previous rate.
By about May 12, 1930, the majority of pork
shops and stalls were unable to continue business
through lack of stock and unless unforeseen circumstances
make it possible for a compromise (a matter generally
held as quite unlikely) to be reached between the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" and the local pig hongs,
local pork shops will be unable to do further business

in a few days.

Local slaughter houses suspend operations

Although the "Southern & Northern District Pig
Hong Traders' Joint Office" and its members have pledged
themselves to a policy of non-cooperation with the
"Shanghai Livestock Market", confidential information
has revealed that immediately after the shortage of
pork was keenly felt, a number of pig hongs who may or
may not be among those who pledged their word against
cooperation, were known to have secretly secured permits
(which could only be done after registration with the
Branch Office of the "Market" at Room 127, Embankment
Building, 400 Soochow Road) from the authorities of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" to make transactions in
Hongkew in order to supply the demands in the two foreign-
controlled areas south of the Soochow Creek. Thus a
fair number of pigs have found their way into the
Settlement. These pigs coming from Hongkew were taken
to the slaughter houses, which at that time were still
carrying on business as usual. On May 6, 1939, however,
the See Sih (蘇錫) and Sing Hing Hai(新亨海)
Slaughter Houses, situated respectively at Lane 1650,
Houses 48 and 50, Chengtu Road, both received threatening
letters purporting to have emanated from some secret
patriotic organization warning them against slaughtering
such pigs.

On May 12, 1939, these slaughter houses signified
their intention of suspending operations on May 13, 1939,
as they were unwilling to slaughter pigs from Hongkew.
Suspension of operations was effected as declared, on the
pages.zh:

数日内。

本地屠宰场停止营业

尽管“南北区猪行联合办事处”及其成员已承诺采取不与“上海牲畜市场”合作的政策，但机密情报显示，在猪肉短缺现象变得严峻之后，一些猪行（无论其是否曾承诺不合作）已知悉秘密从“上海牲畜市场”当局获取了许可证，以便在虹口进行交易，从而供应苏州河以南两个外侨控制区域的需求。因此，相当数量的生猪得以进入租界。这些来自虹口的生猪被送往当时仍照常营业的屠宰场。然而，1939年5月6日，位于成都路1650弄48号和50号的苏锡（See Sih）和新亨海（Sing Hing Hai）两家屠宰场均收到恐吓信，信件声称出自某个秘密爱国组织，警告他们不得屠宰此类生猪。

1939年5月12日，这些屠宰场表示有意于1939年5月13日停止营业，因为它们不愿屠宰来自虹口的生猪。正如所声明的那样，停业措施于1939年5月13日早晨生效，法租界的屠宰场也随即效仿。

Subsequent development and present situation
regarding the pork market

Following the suspension of operation of the
three above mentioned slaughter houses, the local
pork shops and stall keepers, with the exception of
a few who were still carrying on with what little remain-
ing stock they had, appeared to be out of stock although
their shops remained open throughout the day.

On the other hand, notwithstanding the general
clamour of pig dealers for non-cooperation, the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" has been able to proceed
with registering pig dealers who were willing to submit
to its control. Enquiries at the Branch Office of the
Market in Room 127, Embankment Building, 400 North
Soochow Road, revealed that in order to offset the
inconvenience caused by the continued suspension of
operation by the three major slaughter houses in the
Settlement and the French Concession, the authorities
of the "Livestock Market" have decided to slaughter
pigs in the Municipal Abattoir on Dixwell Road from
May 15, 1939, and deliver them to pork shops. The
"Livestock Market" authorities have also been endeavouring
to secure passes for the Hongkew Area, on behalf of the
pork dealers who have registered, in order to enable
them to proceed to the Municipal Abattoir.

On May 15, 1939, some 50 carcasses of pigs were
actually delivered to the Soochow Road Market by the
"Shanghai Livestock Market". The pigs were sold to the
stall holders in the presence of a party of Municipal
Police and no untoward incident occurred.

关于猪肉市场的后续发展及现状

在上述三家屠宰场停止营业后，本地的肉铺和摊贩，除了少数仍在处理剩余少量库存者外，尽管店铺全天开门，但似乎已无货可供。

另一方面，尽管猪商们普遍呼吁不合作，“上海牲畜市场”仍能够继续为愿意接受其控制的猪商办理注册。经向位于北苏州路400号堤岸大厦127室的市场分支机构查询得知，为了弥补公共租界和法租界三大屠宰场持续停业造成的不便，“牲畜市场”当局决定自1939年5月15日起，在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）的市立屠宰场屠宰生猪，并配送至肉铺。“牲畜市场”当局还一直在努力为已注册的猪商争取进入虹口区域的通行证，以便他们能够前往市立屠宰场。

1939年5月15日，“上海牲畜市场”实际向苏州路市场交付了约50头猪 carcasses（胴体）。在一队工部局警察的在场监督下，生猪被出售给摊主，未发生任何意外事件。

According to information obtained from the
branch office of the "Shanghai Livestock Market,"
the number of pork shops which have registered with
the "Shanghai Livestock Market" has shown an increase
and the number of pigs slaughtered at the municipal
abattoir, north of the Creek, and delivered south of
the Creek, has likewise risen.
In the light of the events which have transpired
since the suspension of operations of slaughter houses
and pork shops as dealers, enquiries have been conducted
regarding the attitude of the majority of local pork
dealers who have thus far refused to yield to the
arbitrary measures of the "Livestock Market" authorities,
and it has been ascertained that in the main they are
still determined to adhere to the principle of non-
cooperation. This is corroborated by the fact that
although quantities of pork have been brought from
Hongkew to areas south of the Creek by persons of
doubtful origin, the pork shops and dealers have refused
to accept them. They are stated to have made up their
mind to stand a loss in business until the issue
between the parties in dispute has been settled.
It has been learned that the majority of
the pork dealers in the French Concession intend to
create trouble if the stall holders in the Nanking
Road Market continue to purchase pork from the
"Shanghai Livestock Market." The dealers in the
French Concession cannot sell pork which does not bear
the chop of the P.M.D., C.S.F., and are therefore
unable to purchase pigs from the "Shanghai Livestock
Market", as are the dealers in the Settlement.
In all there are approximately 53 pig hongs, of
which 34 are situated in the Settlement and the remainder
in the French Concession, while there are approximately

鉴于屠宰场和作为经销商的肉铺停业以来所发生的事件，有关部门对大多数至今拒绝屈服于“牲畜市场”当局专断措施的本地猪商的态度进行了调查，并查明他们总体上仍决心坚持不合作原则。以下事实佐证了这一点：尽管有来源可疑的人员将大量猪肉从虹口运至河南岸地区，但肉铺和经销商拒绝接收。据称，他们已下定决心承受业务损失，直到争端各方之间的问题得到解决。

据悉，如果南京路市场的摊主继续从“上海牲畜市场”购买猪肉，法租界的大多数猪商打算制造麻烦。法租界的经销商无法销售没有法租界公董局警务处（P.M.D., C.S.F.）印章的猪肉，因此像租界内的经销商一样，他们无法从“上海牲畜市场”购买生猪。

**Fresh arrivals from Kempo**

As all the slaughter houses in the Settlement
and French Concession have already suspended operations,
recent arrivals of pigs from Kempo, reaching Shanghai
in foreign-owned vessels, are at present being held
in the piggeries. On May 14, some 500 pigs arrived
in Shanghai (south of the Creek) from Kempo in foreign
owned vessels. These pigs, together with those
already in Shanghai, are being kept in the following

**来自金波（Kempo）的新到生猪**

由于租界和法租界的所有屠宰场均已停止营业，近期从金波（Kempo）经由外籍船只运抵上海的生目前正被滞留在养猪场。5月14日，约500头生猪从金波经由外籍船只抵达上海（河南岸）。这些生猪连同已在上海的生正被安置在以下地点，以待现有纠纷最终解决：-

MEMORANDUM ON THE LOCAL PIG TRADE

Local situation prior to the recent establish-
ment of the "Shanghai Livestock Market"

Sometime following the outbreak of local hostilities
the areas adjacent to the International Settlement and
the French Concession in which the majority of the local
pig hongs were located, were rendered inaccessible to
local pig traders and in consequence the latter had had
some, though not serious difficulty in securing fresh
stock for the local market. With the withdrawal of the
Chinese forces from the Shanghai area and the subsequent
general improvement in the local situation, a continuous
supply of pigs from Kompo was maintained without inter-
ruption. The usual source of supply of pigs for local
consumption has been the northern and western parts of
the Yangtsze Delta at which places the local pig hongs
have stationed brokers as their agents for the purpose of
making purchases of stock and arranging their trans-
portation down river. Throughout the ensuing period
of approximately one year and up to the Spring of 1939,
the demand for pork in the foreign controlled areas was
met in a satisfactory manner by local merchants engaged
in this field of trade, while the price of pork was
maintained at a reasonable level. In the early
part of April, 1939, the pig hong owners and the various
steamship companies alike began to experience difficulties
in the business of transporting pigs from Singheong, a
small river port in Kompo. The Japanese authorities
in this area commenced control of the transportation of
pages.zh:
关于本地猪业贸易的备忘录

“上海牲畜市场”最近成立之前的本地局势

在当地战事爆发后不久，国际租界和法租界附近的大部分本地猪行所在区域变得无法通行，导致本地猪商在为本地市场获取新鲜货源方面遇到了一些困难，尽管并不严重。随着中国军队撤离上海地区以及随后当地局势的普遍改善，来自金波（Kompo）的生猪供应得以持续不断。本地消费用生猪的通常来源是长江三角洲的北部和西部地区，本地猪行在这些地方派驻经纪人作为代理，负责采购存货并安排沿河运输。在此后大约一年的时间里，直至1939年春季，外侨控制区域对猪肉的需求由从事该贸易领域的本地商人令人满意地予以满足，同时猪肉价格保持在合理水平。1939年4月上旬，猪行老板和各轮船公司开始在从金波的一个小河港新宏（Singheong）运输生猪的业务中遇到困难。该地区的日本当局开始控制

The people mentioned above are known to have secured
the premises No. 19-21 Miller Road (Hongkew District)
where, on January 1st, 1939, an attempt was made to
establish a monopoly under the title of the Yoong Foong
Company (□□□). The attempt proved a complete

so far reveal there is no connection between the defunct
Yoong Foong Company and the present "Shanghai Livestock

The formation of the "Shanghai
Livestock Market."

Owing to lack of necessary data concerning the
establishment of this organ, the exact date of the
formation of the "Shanghai Livestock Market" cannot be
ascertained with any degree of accuracy and it is held
probable that it came into existence without formal
procedure. This "Market" first attracted the attention
of the Municipal Police on April 10, 1939, when a branch
office was established in Room 127, Embankment Building,
400 North Soochow Road.

On April 12, two notices were published in the
"Eastern Times," one of which stated that the market
would commence functioning on April 15, at the temporary
address of 52 Yochow Road, and that a permanent market
was being built at the corner of Chaoufoong and Vuh Hwa
Roads (O.O.L.). The other notice stated that as from
April 15, 1939, the market would be the sole agency
for the transportation and sale of all kinds of livestock
and instructed pig dealers, livestock brokers and
boatmen engaged in the transportation of livestock to
register with the market between April 16 and 30.

Enquiries made at the branch office of this "Shanghai
Livestock Market" in the Embankment Building show that
it is promoted and operated by a Japanese named Matsuhara
(
pages.zh:
(3)

已知上述人员获得了米勒路（Miller Road，虹口区）19-21号的房产，并于1939年1月1日试图以永丰公司（Yoong Foong Company，□□□）的名义建立垄断。该尝试彻底失败，1939年1月6日，该场所关闭，项目被完全放弃。目前的调查显示，已解散的永丰公司与当前的“上海牲畜市场”之间没有任何联系。

“上海牲畜市场”的成立

由于缺乏关于该机构成立的必要数据，无法准确确定“上海牲畜市场”的确切成立日期，据信其成立可能未经过正式程序。该“市场”首次引起工部局警务处的注意是在1939年4月10日，当时其在北苏州路400号堤岸大厦127室设立了一个分支机构。

4月12日，《东方时报》刊登了两则公告，其中一则声明市场将于4月15日开始运作，临时地址为耀州路（Yochow Road）52号，并在兆丰路（Chaoufoong）和物华路（Vuh Hwa Roads）（O.O.L.）拐角处建设永久性市场。另一则公告声明，自1939年4月15日起，该市场将成为所有种类牲畜运输和销售的唯一代理机构，并指示猪商、牲畜经纪人和从事牲畜运输的船夫在4月16日至30日期间向市场注册。

对在堤岸大厦的“上海牲畜市场”分支机构进行的查询显示，该市场由一名名为松原（Matsuhara）的日本人推动和运营（

pages.en:
(4)
( 王升 ) with a Chinese named Wong Ts-Jang ( 王之江 ),
acting as the Manager, who claim to have secured the
necessary permission from the Japanese Military
Authorities and the "Reformed Government."

With regard to the address at 5. Yochow Road,
enquiries show that prior to the local hostilities
this site was occupied by the Ning Woo Dzu Shing
( 寧屠宰 ) Slaughter House and recently by the Chang
Shun ( 長順 ) Trading Company which deals in pigs.
The Head Office is at 314 Ningpo Road and is operated
by a number of Formosans namely Messrs. Chow Sih-yau
( 周錫 ) and Ling Hwei-nan ( 林南 ) and a number of
Chinese including Mr. Yang Fu-zung ( 楊輔臣 ), owner of
the Tuh Loong ( 德隆行 ) Pig Hong, 21 Vee nou Li, Rue
Lafayette. These individuals when sounded denied
knowledge of the new Livestock Market. In this
connection, lengthy enquiries were conducted at the
branch office in the Embankment Building and information
was obtained that negotiations were then still in
progress between the market authorities and the Japanese
Military Police for the transfer of the lease of 5.
Yochow Road to the Market.

A visit has been made to the site of the proposed
permanent market at the corner of Chaoufeong Road and
Vuh H Road but no sign of construction work was
observed.

Object of the "Shanghai Livestock
Market."

In forming the "Shanghai Livestock Market," the
Japanese and Chinese authorities behind the project
are understood to have cherished the hope of eventually
effecting a monopoly in the Shanghai pig trade. Their
pages.zh:
(4)
（王升）与一名名为王之江（Wong Ts-Jang）的华人，担任经理，声称已获得日本军方当局及“维新政府”的必要许可。

关于扬州路5号的地址，经查询显示，在当地战事爆发前，该址由宁屠宰场（Ning Woo Dzu Shing Slaughter House）占用，近期则由经营生猪生意的长顺（Chang Shun）贸易公司占用。总公司位于宁波路314号，由数名台湾人经营，即周锡（Chow Sih-yau）先生和林南（Ling Hwei-nan）先生，以及数名华人，包括位于拉斐德路（Rue Lafayette）威诺里（Vee nou Li）21号的德隆行（Tuh Loong Pig Hong）猪行老板杨辅臣（Yang Fu-zung）先生。经试探询问，这些人均否认知晓新的牲畜市场一事。就此而言，在外滩大厦的分办事处进行了 lengthy enquiries（冗长查询），获得的信息表明，市场当局与日本宪兵队之间仍在就扬州路5号租赁权转让给市场一事进行谈判。

已前往兆丰路（Chaoufeong Road）与吴淞路（Vuh H Road）转角处拟建的永久性市场工地视察，但未观察到任何施工迹象。

“上海牲畜市场”的目的。

在组建“上海牲畜市场”时，据信该项目背后的日方和中方当局怀有最终垄断上海生猪贸易的希望。他们的

pages.en:
(5)
suggested measures for the registration of pig brokers,
dealers and boatmen at the Registration Office at its
branch office in Room No. 127, Embankment Building, 400
North Soochow Road, between April 18 and 30 and later
extended to May 31, 1939, can only be assumed to be a
preliminary step towards the enforcement of a monopoly
which, it is said, will be effected from June 1, 1939.

Reaction of those affected
by the new project

When it became publicly known that a Japanese
sponsored "Shanghai Livestock Market" was in the course
of formation in the early part of April, 1939, apprehen-
sion was apparent among the local pig traders who could
foresee the trade being adversely affected and all
sorts of impositions being imposed.

Before dealing with the steps taken by the local
pig dealers in opposition to the measures of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" directed at the collection
of a levy on pigs, it is proposed to review briefly
the present situation in the local pig trade as follows:-

There are two markets: one, the so-called Northern
District (Settlement) Market located at 275 Penang Road,
and the other, the so-called Southern District (French
Concession) Market located at 311 Rue Pere Pree. These
two markets have a joint delivery office in Room 205,
264 Kiangse Road and have control of 53 pig hongs.

The Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao, closed
on the outbreak of hostilities. The pig dealers
belonging this guild, are, however, maintaining without
much publicity, a "Southern & Northern District Pig
Hong Traders' Joint Office" in the residence of a
lawyer named Chang Yih 張翼 ), 1 Liang Jing Tsung,
Rue Lafayette. Mr. Chang was secretary to the now
defunct Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao, and
pages.zh:
(5)
建议措施要求猪经纪、商贩和船夫于1939年4月18日至30日期间（后延长至5月31日），在北苏州路400号外滩大厦127室的分办事处登记处进行登记，这只能被视为实施垄断的初步步骤，据说该垄断将于1939年6月1日起生效。

受新项目影响者的反应

当1939年4月初，由日本人赞助的“上海牲畜市场”正在组建的消息公开后，当地猪商中明显出现担忧情绪，他们预见到贸易将受到不利影响，并将被强加各种苛捐杂税。

在详述当地猪商为反对“上海牲畜市场”征收生猪税的措施所采取的步骤之前，拟简要回顾当地生猪贸易的现状如下：

现有两个市场：一个是所谓的北区（租界）市场，位于槟榔路275号；另一个是所谓的南区（法租界）市场，位于神父路（Rue Pere Pree）311号。这两个市场在江西路264号205室设有联合交货处，并控制着53家猪行。

位于南市四高邦（Sih Ka Pang）的猪行公所在战事爆发时关闭。然而，属于该公所的猪商们在不事张扬的情况下，维持着一个“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”，地点位于拉斐德路良精宗（Liang Jing Tsung）1号的一位名为张翼（Chang Yih）的律师寓所内。张先生曾是现已解散的南市四高邦猪行公所的秘书，且

pages.en:
(6)
a staff employee of the now defunct Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Shanghai City Government.
It should be mentioned that the person Wong Ts-jang,
who assists Mr. Matsuhara in the management of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" as related above, was also
a secretary in the employ of the now defunct Pig Hong
Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao.
As the first step towards the controlling of the
livestock trade, the authorities of the "Shanghai
Livestock Market" in the middle of April, 1939, proceeded
with their plan of enforcing a tax of $2.00 per head on
pigs transported to Shanghai from Kompo which method was
assisted by the Japanese authorities who posted men at
Singkong, Northern Kiangsu, for the purpose of seizing
the pigs in enforcing the tax of $2.00.
On April 13, 1939, a number of local pig hongs held
a meeting in the "Southern & Northern District Pig Hong
Traders' Joint Office," 1 Liang Jing Faung, Rue Lafayette,
to consider counter-measures to be taken against the
enforcement of the new levy by the "Shanghai Livestock
Market." Mr. Hung Wen-kiang(洪文江), Assistant
Manager of the Northern District (Settlement) Pig Market
at 273 Penang Road, who presided, made an announcement
that out of a total of 53 pig hongs, 47 had pledged to
refuse to join the "Bogus Livestock Market." According
to the pledge, in order to fulfil the duties of a Chinese
citizen, the person pledging his word is bound to refuse
to cooperate with the "bogus" establishment and is
willing to submit himself to any punishment should he be
found to have broken his pledge. After discussion,
the following resolutions were reached:-
pages.zh:
(6)
是现已解散的上海市政府社会局的一名职员。
值得一提的是，上述协助松原（Matsuhara）先生管理“上海牲畜市场”的王之江（Wong Ts-jang），也曾是现已解散的南市四高邦猪行公所的秘书。
作为控制牲畜贸易的第一步，“上海牲畜市场”当局于1939年4月中旬着手执行其计划，对从高邮（Kompo）运往上海的生猪每头征收2.00元税款，该方法得到了日本当局的协助，日方在江苏北部的兴孔（Singkong，音译）派驻人员，以扣押生猪的方式强制征收2.00元税款。
1939年4月13日，多家本地猪行在拉斐德路良精坊（Liang Jing Faung，原文如此，前文为良精宗）1号的“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”举行会议，商讨针对“上海牲畜市场”强制征收新税款的对策。主持会议的是位于槟榔路273号的北区（租界）猪市场副经理洪文江（Hung Wen-kiang）先生，他宣布在总共53家猪行中，有47家已承诺拒绝加入“伪牲畜市场”。根据承诺，为了履行中国公民的职责，做出承诺者必须拒绝与“伪”机构合作，并愿意在违背承诺时接受任何惩罚。经讨论，达成以下决议：

pages.en:
(7)
(1) That a committee of seven persons including Mr. Hung
Wen-kiang and Mr. Chang Yih be formed to take safe
custody of the pledges.
(2) That a manifesto containing the decision of the pig
hongs to refuse to join the "Livestock Market" be
published in the Chinese press.
(3) That should the "Livestock Market" insist on a
monopoly, all of the 47 pig hongs who had pledged
their word should suspend business rather than submit.
Following this meeting, a circular was issued on
April 23, 1939, in the name of the old Pig Hong Guild by
the "Southern & Northern District Pig Hong Traders' Joint
Office mentioned above, to local pig hongs, urging them
to insist on non-cooperation with the "Shanghai Livestock
Market."
On April 18, 1939, in pursuance of one of the
resolutions adopted at the above meeting, the pig traders
inserted a notice in the Chinese press reaffirming their
attitude and urging members to stand against cooperation
with any "illegal organizations."
Towards the end of April and in the early part
of May, 1939, cases continued to come to light in which
various consignments of pigs arriving from Kiangsu were
intercepted on the Whangpoo and later unloaded and detained
in Hongkew by persons claiming to be officials of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market." Negotiations were once
stated to have taken place between the Nisshin Kisen
Kaisha, which was responsible for the transportation
of some of these consignments, and the individual pig
hongs to which the pigs were said to belong, but no
tangible results are known to have been achieved and
a shortage of pork ensued.
In view of the repeated interference with the
arrival of pigs from Kiangsu by the Japanese-sponsored
"Shanghai Livestock Market," a number of local pig
pages.zh:
(7)
(1) 成立一个由七人组成的委员会，其中包括洪文江先生和张翼先生，负责妥善保管承诺书。
(2) 在中文报刊上发表宣言，载明各猪行拒绝加入“牲畜市场”的决定。
(3) 如果“牲畜市场”坚持垄断，所有47家已做出承诺的猪行应停业而非屈服。
会议结束后，上述“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”于1939年4月23日以旧猪行公所的名义向本地各猪行发出通函，敦促他们坚持不与“上海牲畜市场”合作。
1939年4月18日，根据上述会议通过的一项决议，猪商们在中文报刊上刊登通告，重申其立场，并敦促成员抵制与任何“非法组织”合作。
1939年4月底至5月初，陆续发生多起事件，从江苏运抵的各批生猪在黄浦江上被拦截，随后被自称是“上海牲畜市场”官员的人员卸货并扣留在虹口。据称，负责运输部分这批货物的日清汽船株式会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）曾与据称拥有这些生猪的各猪行进行谈判，但据悉未取得任何实质性成果，导致猪肉短缺。
鉴于由日本人赞助的“上海牲畜市场”反复干扰从江苏运抵的生猪，多名本地猪

pages.en:
(8)

dealers held a meeting in the Southern District Pig
Market on May 2, at which counter-measures were discussed
and the following decisions were adopted at this meeting:-
(1) That pig dealers should persist in their opposition
to the collection of taxes and that they should
sacrifice their business rather than attempt a
compromise under threats.
(2) That in future, the pig hong owners shall equally
share the losses sustained by any of their members
as the result of interference in the transportation
of pigs. Those who secretly compromise should be
severely punished.
(3) That the pig hongs would cease to transport pigs
from Kompo should threats be made to control the
pig trade by compulsory means.
(4) That letters in the name of the Pig Hong Guild be
sent to the Shanghai Municipal Council and the
C.M.F., and the Ratepayers' Associations to request
assistance.

Under these circumstances, the local pig hong
owners despatched telegrams to their brokers and agencies
in Northern Kiangsu advising them to cease the
transportation of pigs pending a final settlement of
the present controversy. In consequence arrivals of
pigs have been greatly curtailed and this has in turn
caused the price of pork to rise to $1.00 per catty,
which amounts to an increase of about 40 per cent
compared with the previous rate.

By about May 12, 1939, the majority of pork
shops and stalls were unable to continue business
through lack of stock and unless unforeseen circumstances
make it possible for a compromise (a matter generally
held as quite unlikely) to be reached between the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" and the local pig hongs,
local pork shops will be unable to do further business
pages.zh:
(8)

商于5月2日在南区猪市场举行会议，讨论对策，并在会上通过以下决定：
(1) 猪商应坚持反对征税，宁愿牺牲生意，也不在威胁下寻求妥协。
(2) 今后，若任何成员因生猪运输受干扰而遭受损失，各猪行老板应共同分担。秘密妥协者将受到严厉惩罚。
(3) 如果以强制手段控制生猪贸易的威胁成为现实，各猪行将停止从高邮运输生猪。
(4) 以猪行公所的名义致函上海公共租界工部局、法公董局（C.M.F.）及纳税人协会，请求援助。

在此情况下，本地猪行老板向其位于江苏北部的经纪人和代理机构发送电报，建议在当前争议最终解决之前停止生猪运输。因此，生猪抵达量大幅减少，进而导致猪肉价格涨至每斤1.00元，较之前的价格涨幅约为40%。

截至1939年5月12日左右，大多数肉铺和摊位因缺乏库存而无法继续营业，除非出现不可预见的情况，使“上海牲畜市场”与本地猪行之间达成妥协（普遍认为这极不可能），否则本地肉铺将在几天内无法继续营业

pages.en:
(9)

in a few days.

Local slaughter houses suspend operations

Although the "Southern & Northern District Pig
Hong Traders' Joint Office" and its members have pledged
themselves to a policy of non-cooperation with the
"Shanghai Livestock Market", confidential information
has revealed that immediately after the shortage of
pork was keenly felt, a number of pig hongs who may or
may not be among those who pledged their word against
cooperation, were known to have secretly secured permits
(which could only be done after registration with the
Branch Office of the "Market" at Room 127, Embankment
Building, 400 Soochow Road) from the authorities of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" to make transactions in
Hongkew in order to supply the demands in the two foreign-
controlled areas south of the Soochow Creek. Thus a
fair number of pigs have found their way into the
Settlement. These pigs coming from Hongkew were taken
to the slaughter houses, which at that time were still
carrying on business as usual. On May 6, 1939, however,
the See Sih (蘇錫) and Sing Ning Hai (新寧海)
Slaughter Houses, situated respectively at Lane 1050,
Houses 48 and 50, Chengtu Road, both received threatening
letters purporting to have emanated from some secret
patriotic organization warning them against slaughtering
such pigs.

On May 12, 1939, these slaughter houses signified
their intention of suspending operations on May 13, 1939,
as they were unwilling to slaughter pigs from Hongkew.
Suspension of operations was effected as declared, on the
pages.zh:
(9)

。

本地屠宰场暂停运营

尽管“南北区猪行商人联合办事处”及其成员已承诺采取不与“上海牲畜市场”合作的政策，但机密情报显示，就在猪肉短缺感强烈之际，已知有一些猪行（无论其是否属于那些承诺不合作的行列）秘密从“上海牲畜市场”当局获得了许可证（只有在该市场位于苏州路400号外滩大厦127室的分办事处注册后才能获得），以便在虹口进行交易，从而供应苏州河以南两个外籍管制区域的需求。因此，相当数量的生猪得以进入租界。这些来自虹口的生猪被送往屠宰场，当时这些屠宰场仍照常营业。然而，1939年5月6日，分别位于成都路1050弄48号和50号的苏锡（See Sih）和新宁海（Sing Ning Hai）屠宰场均收到恐吓信，信件 purportedly（据称）出自某个秘密爱国组织，警告他们不得屠宰此类生猪。

1939年5月12日，这些屠宰场表示有意于1939年5月13日暂停运营，因为他们不愿屠宰来自虹口的生猪。正如所声明的那样，暂停运营于

pages.en:
(10)
morning of May 13, 1939, with the Slaughter House in
the French Concession following suit.

Subsequent development and present situation
regarding the pork market

Following the suspension of operation of the
three above mentioned slaughter houses, the local
pork shops and stall keepers, with the exception of
a few who were still carrying on with what little remain-
ing stock they had, appeared to be out of stock although
their shops remained open throughout the day.

On the other hand, notwithstanding the general
clamour of pig dealers for non-cooperation, the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" has been able to proceed
with registering pig dealers who were willing to submit
to its control. Enquiries at the Branch Office of the
Market in Room 127, Embankment Building, 400 North
Soochow Road, revealed that in order to offset the
inconvenience caused by the continued suspension of
operation by the three major slaughter houses in the
Settlement and the French Concession, the authorities
of the "Livestock Market" have decided to slaughter
pigs in the Municipal Abattoir on Dixwell Road from
May 15, 1939, and deliver them to pork shops. The
"Livestock Market" authorities have also been endeavouring
to secure passes for the Hongkew Area, on behalf of the
pork dealers who have registered, in order to enable
them to proceed to the Municipal Abattoir.

On May 15, 1939, some 30 carcasses of pigs were
actually delivered to the Soochow Road Market by the
"Shanghai Livestock Market". The pigs were sold to the
stall holders in the presence of a party of Municipal
Police and no untoward incident occurred.
pages.zh:
(10)
1939年5月13日上午生效，法租界的屠宰场也随即效仿。

后续发展及猪肉市场现状

在上述三家屠宰场暂停运营后，本地肉铺和摊主除了少数仍依靠剩余少量库存维持营业者外，似乎已无货可供，尽管他们的店铺全天开门。

另一方面，尽管猪商们普遍呼吁不合作，“上海牲畜市场”仍得以继续为愿意服从其控制的猪商办理登记。对市场位于北苏州路400号外滩大厦127室的分办事处的查询显示，为了抵消租界和法租界三大屠宰场持续暂停运营造成的不便，“牲畜市场”当局决定自1939年5月15日起在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）的市立屠宰场屠宰生猪，并配送给肉铺。“牲畜市场”当局还一直努力为已登记的猪肉经销商获取进入虹口区域的通行证，以便他们能够前往市立屠宰场。

1939年5月15日，“上海牲畜市场”实际向苏州路市场交付了约30具猪 carcasses（胴体）。在一队巡捕的在场监督下，生猪被出售给摊主，未发生任何意外事件。

pages.en:
(11)

According to information obtained from the
Branch office of the "Shanghai Livestock Market,"
the number of pork shops which have registered with
the "Shanghai Livestock Market" has shown an increase
and the number of pigs slaughtered at the Municipal
Abattoir, North of the Creek, and delivered south of
the Creek, has likewise risen.

In the light of the events which have transpired
since the suspension of operations of slaughter houses
and pork shops and dealers, enquiries have been conducted
regarding the attitude of the majority of local pork
dealers who have thus far refused to yield to the
arbitrary measures of the "Livestock Market" authorities,
and it has been ascertained that in the main they are
still determined to adhere to the principle of non-
cooperation. This is corroborated by the fact that
although quantities of pork have been brought from
Hongkew to areas south of the Creek by persons of
doubtful origin, the pork shops and dealers have refused
to accept them. They are stated to have made up their
mind to stand a loss in business until the issue
between the parties in dispute has been settled.

It has been learned that the majority of
the pork dealers in the French Concession intend to
create trouble if the stall holders in the Foochow
Road Market continue to purchase pork from the
"Shanghai Livestock Market." The dealers in the
French Concession cannot sell pork which does not bear
the chop of the P.M.D., C.M.P., and are therefore
unable to purchase pigs from the "Shanghai Livestock
Market", as are the dealers in the Settlement.

In all there are approximately 85 pig houses, of
which 34 are situated in the Settlement and the remainder
in the French Concession, while there are approximately

鉴于自屠宰场、肉铺及商贩停业以来所发生的事件，已就迄今拒绝屈服于“牲畜市场”当局专断措施的大多数本地猪肉商的态度进行了调查，并查明他们主要仍决心坚持不合作原则。以下事实佐证了这一点：尽管有身份可疑之人将大量猪肉从虹口运至苏州河以南地区，但肉铺和商贩均拒绝接收。据称，他们已下定决心承受业务损失，直至争议各方之间的问题得到解决。

As a result of the repeated interference with
the arrival of pigs from Kompo by the Japanese
sponsored "Shanghai Livestock Market" which has
resulted in the present shortage of pigs and the
subsequent increase in the price of pork in the local
market, the local situation regarding the supply of
pork is becoming daily more acute and the various
stall-keepers and shops dealing in pork in the
Settlement have found it impossible to continue their
business. The object of the authorities of the
"Shanghai Livestock Market" in interfering with the
transportation of pigs from the interior to Shanghai,
south of the Soochow Creek, is to retaliate against
the obstinate stand taken by the majority of the
local pig dealers in opposition to the arbitrary
measures directed at the collection of a levy on
pigs by the "Shanghai Livestock Market."

In the beginning of April, 1939, the "Shanghai
Livestock Market" established a branch office at
Room 127, Embankment Building, 400 North Soochow Road
and published two notices in the local press (the
"Eastern Times") which were to the effect that the
"Market" would commence functioning on April 15, 1939
and that all dealers were instructed to join and
register with the Market which would, as from April
15, 1939, be the sole agency for the transportation of

and a decision was also reached to the effect that

MAY 12 1939

Pork Famine Threatened
in Shanghai
Pig Dealers Refuse to
Meet Regulations
Shanghai will go porkless tomor-
row for unless some pork dealers try
to buy secretly from the newly estab-
lished Japanese sponsored Shanghai
Cattle Market in Hongkew against
which pork dealers have declared a
go-slow strike there will be no pork
at all for sale.
The decision for declaring the strike
was reached yesterday at a meeting
attended by members of the Shanghai
Pork Dealers Association and it is
understood that notices warning all
pork dealers against continuing their
business will be distributed to-day.
Because of this procedure informed
quarters believed that some pork
dealers might continue their busi-
ness today with a limited supply at
their disposal.
It was expected by the same quar-
ters yesterday that there might be
no pork for sale at all tomorrow
unless "traitors" try to obtain pork
from Hongkew secretly in order to
get a big profit.
The strike will be called as a protest
against the monopoly of the pig trans-
portation business by the new market,
which has declared that all pig
dealers must register with it
and that all steamers carry-
ing pigs to Shanghai must be sanc-
tioned. Disobeying the regulations,
pig dealers doing business south of
the creek have not registered and
consequently several shipments of pigs
they bought have been detained.

上海面临猪肉荒
猪商拒绝遵守规定
除非一些猪肉商试图从新成立的、由日本人支持的位于虹口的上海牲畜市场秘密购买——对此猪肉商已宣布实行怠工罢工——否则上海明天将无猪肉可售。
宣布罢工的决定是昨天在上海猪肉商协会成员参加的会议上作出的，据悉，警告所有猪肉商不要继续营业的通知将于今天分发。

同一批知情人士昨天预计，除非“汉奸”为了获取暴利而试图从虹口秘密获取猪肉，否则明天可能根本无猪肉可售。
此次罢工旨在抗议新市场对生猪运输业务的垄断，该市场已宣布所有猪商必须向其注册，且所有运载生猪至上海的轮船必须获得批准。违反规定，在苏州河以南经商的猪商未进行注册，因此他们购买的几批生猪已被扣押。

SHANGHAI TIMES,
MAY 12 1939

PIGS REMOVED FROM
BRITISH VESSEL

Military Interfere With
Shipment; Decision
Reached To Unload

The Jardine Matheson coastal vessel, s.s. Tungwo, on mission of transporting 490 pigs from Hsingkong to Shanghai last Monday, encountered difficulties with a Japanese military party who protested against the British vessel transporting the pigs. Much discussion ensued, following which the cargo of pork was returned to the shore by Captain Blacquiere, and to the owners by the Jardine Matheson Company, agents at this port.

At 5 p.m. on Tuesday a radio message from the ship was received here stating that the s.s. Tungwo had been prevented from sailing with the pigs. Another message had been sent to the British gunboat H.M.S. Scorpion which was on patrol duty in that area with Rear Admiral R. V. Holt on board. The gunboat proceeded to the scene immediately.

Prior to the loading of 490 pigs on the s.s. Tungwo, a Japanese ship had transported some 700 pigs from Hsingkong, leaving the remaining number on the wharf. The British vessel, already 24 hours late on schedule, loaded the pigs but was ordered by the military group to unload them. The Jardine Matheson agents on shore, fearing future reprisals against them, acted on their own initiative, and requested the captain to unload the cargo, and this request was complied with. Shortly afterwards the Tungwo sailed without the pigs and H.M.S. Scorpion resumed her duties.

《上海泰晤士报》，
1939年5月12日

生猪从英国船只卸下

军方干涉装运；决定卸货

怡和洋行的沿海轮船“同和”轮（s.s. Tungwo），上周执行从兴港（Hsingkong）向上海运输490头生猪的任务时，遭遇日本军方的阻挠，后者抗议英国船只运输生猪。随后进行了大量讨论，之后船长Blacquiere将猪肉货物退回岸上，并由该港口代理商怡和洋行交还给货主。

周二下午5点，此处收到来自该船的无线电消息，称“同和”轮被阻止载运生猪起航。另一条消息已发送给在该区域巡逻且载有R. V. Holt少将的英国炮舰“蝎子”号（H.M.S. Scorpion）。炮舰立即赶赴现场。

在490头生猪装上“同和”轮之前，一艘日本船只已从兴港运走约700头生猪，留下剩余数量在码头上。这艘英国轮船已比预定时间晚24小时，虽装上了生猪，但被军方团体命令卸下。岸上的怡和洋行代理商因担心日后遭到报复，主动采取行动，请求船长卸下货物，该请求得到了遵从。不久后，“同和”轮未载生猪启航，“蝎子”号恢复了其职责。

with an office in Room 127 Embankment Building,
400 North Soochow Road, issued a notification to
the effect that the registration of pig brokers for
the first period concluded on May 10 and that
further registration will be announced after the
completion of the formation of the whole livestock

doing business since May 1, selling quantities of
pork to shops in the Settlement north of the

shops in that area south of the Soochow Creek.
Following lack of supplies in this part of the

market for pigs and the number sold to those shops
south of the Creek increased to 800 on May 12.

pigs arrived from Kompo by two boats of the Nisshin
Kisen Kaisha, but before unloading at French
Concession were held up in the Whangpoo and taken
to a wharf at Hongkew by officials of the Japanese
sponsored "Shanghai Livestock Market," as a means
to enforce their levy.

are said to be also reluctant to cooperate with the
so-called "Shanghai Livestock Market," with the
result that the arrival of pigs in Shanghai has
recently been curtailed. It is believed that the
situation will not improve until a settlement of

5月7日下午，约600头生猪由日清汽船株式会社的两艘船只从高邮（Kompo）运抵，但在法租界卸货前，在黄浦江被拦下，并被日本支持的“上海牲畜市场”官员带至虹口的一处码头，以此作为强制征收其税费的手段。

尽管日方反复试图以收税的形式控制贸易，但本地猪行老板（共53家）拒绝屈服，据说高邮的猪商也不愿与所谓的“上海牲畜市场”合作，导致近期运抵上海的生猪数量减少。相信在该问题得到友好解决之前，局势不会改善。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
MAY 5 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8039A/50
Date 5 5 39

Pig Dealers Make
Complaint
Foreign Authorities Asked
To Check Monopoly by
New Hongkew Market

Asserting that they have been deprived of the right of "free trade" in the foreign settlements, the Shanghai Pig Dealers Association has forwarded two official letters to the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Municipal Council of the French Concession requesting them to secure a remedy to the difficult situation in which the public may also suffer a shortage of pork as a result of the detention of pigs by the newly-established Shanghai Cattle Market in Hongkew which seeks to monopolize the business.

The dispute between pig dealers and those in charge of the Japanese-sponsored new market, which is already of several weeks' duration, is becoming increasingly serious as now the matter has been officially referred to the administrations in the foreign settlements which have been requested to "uphold their administrative right." The letters hint that merchants dealing in other kinds of cattle and operating south of the creek may suffer also as a result of the monopoly which affects the livelihood of many and which may also constitute a serious menace to public peace and order."

The letters mention the detention of more than 1,000 pigs ordered by the complaining pig dealers who could not take delivery because when the "appointed" Japanese steamers carried them to Shanghai the pigs were detained by the new market authorities. These detained pigs, it was reliably learnt yesterday, have been returned to their buyers, but it was reported that the market authorities still want to collect 40 cents for each pig. The pigs were detained four days ago and as a result the complaining dealers have suffered a loss on which question they have "reserved" the right to negotiate later. When the letters were sent to the authorities about 400 other pigs arriving here by train were again detained.

Meanwhile, the pig dealers have issued a circular notice to pork dealers asking them to maintain their original price, but it is a fact that the price has been increased as the supply has been limited as a result of the controversy.

（批：R / 5/5 / Like / C's）

日期 1939年5月5日

猪商提出
投诉
请求外国当局
制止新虹口市场的垄断行为

上海猪业公会声称其在外国租界内的“自由贸易”权利被剥夺，已向上海工部局和公董局递交两封正式信函，请求他们采取措施补救目前的困难局面，否则公众可能因位于虹口的新建上海牲畜市场扣留生猪、企图垄断业务而面临猪肉短缺。

猪商与日方支持的新市场负责人之间的纠纷已持续数周，随着此事正式提交给外国租界当局并要求其“维护行政权”，局势日益严重。信函暗示，经营其他种类牲畜且在苏州河以南运营的商人也可能因这种垄断而遭受损失，这不仅影响许多人的生计，还可能对公共和平与秩序构成严重威胁。”

信函提到，投诉的猪商无法提货，因为当“指定”的日本轮船将生猪运至上海时，超过1,000头生猪被新市场当局扣留。据可靠消息，这些被扣生猪已于昨日退还给买家，但据报道，市场当局仍要求每头生猪收取40美分。生猪于四天前被扣，导致投诉的经销商遭受损失，他们就此事“保留”日后谈判的权利。当信函送至当局时，另有约400头乘火车抵达此处的生猪再次被扣。

与此同时，猪商已发布通告，要求肉贩维持原价，但事实上，由于争议导致供应受限，价格已经上涨。

（批：R / 5月5日 / Like / C's）

Pig Dealers Boycott
New Market
The price of pork in Shanghai has already been increased and after sometime an acute shortage of pork may be experienced because at an emergency meeting held yesterday executives of the Shanghai Pig Dealers Association decided to suspend business as a protest against the alleged detention of more than 1,000 pigs by the newly established Shanghai Cattle Market in Hongkew in which pig dealers operating south of the creek have refused to participate.
As separate meetings butchers decided not to slaughter any pig sent from the Hongkew market and pork dealers reached a similar "boycott" decision. The Shanghai Municipal Council and Municipal Council of the French Concession will be petitioned for intervention, as both sides to the dispute could not break the deadlock themselves, it was reliably learnt.

Subject Pig Dealers Oppose Collection of Tax by the Japanese
Sponsored "Shanghai Livestock Market"
Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford J.J.

The 1,050 pigs which arrived in Shanghai on
May 1 from Kompo by the "Chiyo Maru" and "Shinko
Maru" were returned to the dealers without the levy
demanded by the officials of the Japanese sponsored
"Shanghai Livestock Market" (Vide Special Branch
report 2-5-39). This settlement was reached
through the efforts of Mr. MATSENMOTO (松本 )
of the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, on whose ships the
pigs were transported to Shanghai.

In view of the repeated interference by
Japanese with the transportation of pigs, six dealers
of the trade held a meeting in the Southern District
Pig Market (French Concession) between 6 p.m. and
7 p.m. May 2, and discussed counter-measures. The
following decisions were passed :-

1. That pig dealers shall persist in their opposition
to the collection of tax, and that they shall
sacrifice their business rather than attempt a
compromise in the face of threats.

2. That in future, the pig hong owners shall
equally share the losses sustained by any
of their members as the result of interference
in the transportation of pigs. Those who
secretly make a compromise shall be severely
dealt with.

3. That the pig hongs will cease to transport pigs
from Kompo should threats be made to control
the trade by compulsory means.

4. That letters in the name of the Pig Hong Guild be
sent to the S.M.C. and C.M.F., and the Ratepayers'
Associations for the purpose of requesting
assistance.

FILE notice to the above effect has been posted in the
Southern District Pig Market, 311 Rue du Pere Froc.
Pan Lien-pih

事由 猪商反对日本扶植的“上海牲畜市场”征税
由 督察员 潘连璧 呈报 经由 C. Crawford J.J. 转呈

5月1日由“千代丸”号和“新光丸”号从汉口（Kompo，音译）运抵上海的1,050头猪，在未缴纳日本扶植的“上海牲畜市场”官员所要求的税款的情况下，被退还给猪商（参见特科报告 2-5-39）。这一结果是通过日清汽船株式会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）的松本（MATSENMOTO）先生的努力达成的，猪正是由该公司的船只运往上海的。

鉴于日本人屡次干扰生猪运输，该行业的六名猪商于5月2日下午6时至7时在南区猪市（法租界）举行会议，商讨对策。通过以下决议：

1. 猪商应坚持反对征税，面对威胁宁可牺牲生意，也不寻求妥协。

2. 今后，若任何成员因生猪运输受干扰而遭受损失，各猪行老板应共同分担。凡私下妥协者，将予以严惩。

3. 若有人以强制手段控制贸易相威胁，各猪行将停止从汉口（Kompo，音译）运输生猪。

4. 以猪行公会名义致函工部局（S.M.C.）、公董局（C.M.F.）及纳税人协会，请求协助。

上述内容的通告已张贴于拉斐特路（Rue du Pere Froc）311号的南区猪市。

Date May 2, 1939.

Subject (in full) Pigs arrived from Kompo - Interference by Japanese

Made by D.I. Pan Lien-pih Forwarded by C. Crawford S.S.

On May 1, about 1,050 pigs arrived in Shanghai from
Kompo by the "Chiyo Maru" and "Shinko Maru" which berthed
on the Pootung side, but were prohibited from unloading,
by officials of the "Shanghai Livestock Market," who
required the dealers to pay a tax of $0.50 each. The
pig dealers are opposed to the levy, and have conducted
negotiations with the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, on whose ships
the pigs were transported to Shanghai, but no settlement
has yet been reached.

On the same day, another 2,000 pigs arrived from
Kompo by boats other than Japanese owned, and were unloaded
without any interference from the Japanese authorities.

Date April 27, 1939.

Subject "Shanghai Livestock Market" - temporary market
being established at 52 Yochow Road.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Crawford. J.J.

A temporary market of the "Shanghai Livestock
Market" is under construction at 52 Yochow Road. The
construction is expected to be completed on April 30
and the market will open for business on May 1. A
signboard "Temporary Address of the Shanghai Livestock
Market" was placed outside the premises on April 25.

The Ning Woo Dzu Shing (寧沪聚兴) Slaughter
House, a Chinese firm, occupied these premises prior to
the hostilities, but they were recently taken over by
the Chang Shun (長順) Trading Company Branch,
Formosan pig dealers. The lease has been transferred
from the Chang Shun to the "Livestock Market" through
arrangements carried out by the Japanese Military Police.

In connection with the intention of the
market to register pig brokers, dealers and boatmen
between April 16 and 30, it has been learned from the
registration office in Room 127 Embankment Building,
400 North Soochow Road, that very little success has
attended those efforts. It is confidentially
learned that the market will prolong the period of
registration to May 31 and enforce the monopoly on
June 1.

are hereby notified again that they must be of one mind

Sin Wan Pao (Evening Edition) of April 22 :-
JAPANESE TO CONTROL PIG MARKET
In an attempt to control the pig trade as from
May 1, the Japanese have formed a Shanghai Livestock Market
on Yochow Road with an office to the north of the Honan Road
Bridge. The "Shanghai-Nanking Pork Trade Company"(滬寧肉業公司)
has established a pig godown and a pig weighing market, of
which Wong Chi-sun (王茂生) is manager and Yang Tsoh-ching
(楊竹卿) is salesman.
It is learned that the Zang Zung (長順),
Van Zung (萬慎) and other pig hongs have promised to join
the market as brokers. The brokers will charge $1 as
commission for each pig, $2 for freight and sundry expenses
and another $2 as controlling fee.
The Japanese will compel pig dealers to
transport pigs by Japanese vessels and to dispose of them
through the market. To achieve this, they will blockade
the Yangtse and the suburbs of Shanghai. Inspection
parties will be despatched to railway stations and wharfs
to take pig dealers to the market.

Subject. Southern & Northern District Pig Hong Traders' Joint Office
- receives threatening letter.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by G. Crawford D. I.

On April 15, the "Southern & Northern District
Pig Hong Traders' Joint Office", 1 Liang Jing Faung
(良勤坊), Rue Lafayette, received through the mail
an annonymous letter warning the pig traders against
taking part in "bogus organization" on pain of drastic
action. It was signed with five crosses.
The "bogus organization" referred to is believed
to be the "Shanghai Livestock Market" with a branch
office in room 127 Embankment Building, 400 North
Soochow Road. It will be recalled that 47 of the
53 pig hongs locally, all members of the "Southern &
Northern District Pig Hong Traders' Joint Office",
pledged a refusal to co-operate with the "Bogus
Livestock Market" (Vide Special Report dated April 15).
On the Chinese press dated April 18, the pig traders
inserted a notice replying to the "five crosses" writer
that the traders' guild and its members prior to the
receipt of the letter pledged to refrain from
co-operating with all "illegal organizations."

4月15日，位于拉斐德路（Rue Lafayette）良勤坊1号的“南北区猪行联合办事处”通过邮件收到一封匿名信，警告猪商不得参与“伪组织”，否则将采取严厉行动。信末签有五个十字叉。

1939

Local Meat Shortage Feared
As Dealers Fight Monopoly

Japanese-Owned Market Takes Drastic Measure
Against Hongs Refusing To Pay Special
Levies On Shipments From Interior

A meat shortage is threatening
the Settlement and Concession as
the squabble between Chinese live
stock dealers and the Japanese-
sponsored cattle market deepened
into a hopeless deadlock, Chinese
reports indicated yesterday.
After a long series of verbal
battles, followed by the hog dealers'
defiant statement of non-co-opera-
tion, the Japanese set-up took
drastic action Tuesday by detaining
several hundred pigs on their
arrival at the North Station.
Seeking the release of their cargo,
the owners of the pigs were in-
formed that a payment of $1.10 per
head would be required before the
release could be allowed.
Payment Made
According to reports, heated
words were exchanged between
agents of the market and the
dealers, but the latter finally
yielded by making the payment on
the condition that a receipt would
be issued to them.
Instead of a receipt duly issued
by the market, the dealers were
said to have been given a certificate
indicating that a specified amount
of money had been paid for the live
stock shipment but bearing no
signatures of the responsible
officials.
Following the incident, a group
of cattle dealers here were reported
to have threatened to stop import-
ing cattle to the Settlement and
Concession from the Japanese oc-
cupied territory.
Statements Expected
Chinese sources indicated that
following the example set by the
pig hongs in the city, firms dealing
in cows, lambs, chicken and ducks
were expected to make a similar
statement in the near future.
The Japanese outfit, headed by
a Japanese, was inaugurated on
April 15. According to its present
ruling, levies on cattle and fowl
imported into the Settlement and
Concession are $2 for each pig, $10
for each cow and 10 cents for each
duck, chicken or goose.
Local traders were of the opinion
that besides attempting to control
the cattle and fowl trade, the Jap-
anese-owned market is giving
special aid to the Japanese steam-
ship companies now operating on
the Yangtse River and the inland
waterways. One of the rulings which
dealers are required to abide by is
that only Japanese vessels might be
used for the transportation of the
live-stock cargo.

因商行抵制垄断，担忧本地肉类短缺

日资市场对拒绝支付内地运货特别捐税的猪行采取严厉措施

据昨日中文报道显示，随着中国牲畜商人与日本支持的牛市之间的争吵陷入无望的僵局，公共租界和法租界正面临肉类短缺的威胁。
经过一系列口头争斗，随后猪商发表 defiant（挑衅/坚决）的不合作声明，日方机构于周二采取严厉行动，在数百头猪抵达北站时将其扣留。
为寻求释放货物，猪主被告知，每头猪需支付1.10美元方可获准放行。
已付款
据报道，市场代理人与商人之间发生了激烈的言语冲突，但后者最终屈服，条件是必须向他们开具收据，才同意付款。
据说，商人并未收到市场正式开具的收据，而是得到了一张证书，表明已为牲畜运输支付了指定金额，但该证书上没有负责官员的签名。
在此事件之后，据报道，本地一群牛商威胁要停止从日军占领区向公共租界和法租界进口牛只。
预计将发表声明
中方消息人士指出，继本市猪行之例，经营牛、羊、鸡和鸭的商号预计在不久的将来也会发表类似声明。
这家由一名日本人领导的日本机构于4月15日正式成立。根据其现行规定，对输入公共租界和法租界的牛羊家禽征收的捐税为：每头猪2美元，每头牛10美元，每只鸭、鸡或鹅10美分。
本地商人认为，除了试图控制牲畜和家禽贸易外，这家日资市场还在特别援助目前在长江及内河航线上运营的日本轮船公司。商人必须遵守的规定之一是，运输牲畜货物只能使用日本船只。

April 19, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Chinese-American Daily News and other local newspapers :-

OPPOSITION TO LIVE STOCK MARKET IN SHANGHAI

Since the inauguration of a Livestock Market by the Shanghai City Government, local hongs and dealers of cattle, sheep, pigs, chickens and ducks and the guilds have refused to join the market. The Japanese and the puppets are planning to control these trades by placing restrictions on means of transportation. They are compelling dealers to transport livestock by Japanese vessels.

The Livestock Market is temporarily located at 52 Tochow Road but has a general office at 400 North Soochow Road. Due to strong opposition from the dealers, the market has done very little business since its formation on April 15. The market is being managed by a Japanese named Matsumoto and a Chinese called Wang Tse-jang (王老強) as sub-manager. Enquiries were made among the various guilds, but none of them knew any man by this name in their trades.

It is also learned that the object of the formation of the market by the puppet organ is to secure full control of the transportation of livestock. Dealers in the interior are compelled to send their cargoes to Shanghai by Japanese vessels and the goods are not allowed to be delivered unless they are taken to the market. A heavy commission of $10 per head of cattle, $2 per pig and $0.10 per fowl is charged.

The various livestock guilds are firmly refusing to co-operate with the Livestock Market. In addition to a joint manifesto issued by local fellow pig hongs, the cattle and sheep dealers are also opposing the market and the entire body of livestock dealers will go to the length of suspending business altogether. As to those who have secretly joined the market, warnings have been sent by patriotic bodies. Pig dealers have ascertained the names of those who have joined the Livestock Market and ways and means are being devised to deal with them.

Yesterday several hundred pigs were sent by train to Shanghai and taken to the Livestock Market in Hongkew. Subsequently, the matter was settled by the payment of $1.10 for each pig. A certificate was issued by the market stating that the necessary procedure had been complied with, and armed persons should allow the pigs to be taken away. The amount of money collected and the name of the responsible person were not mentioned.

The pig dealers are highly indignant and are threatening to cease ordering pigs for Shanghai. In that event there will be a shortage of pork in Shanghai.

1939年4月19日。下午译件。

《中美日报》及其他本地报纸：

反对上海牲畜市场

自上海市政府成立牲畜市场以来，本地的牛、羊、猪、鸡、鸭商行及同业公会均拒绝加入该市场。日本人及傀儡政权正计划通过限制运输手段来控制这些行业。他们强迫商人使用日本船只运输牲畜。

该牲畜市场暂设于周家嘴路（Tochow Road）52号，但在北苏州路400号设有总办事处。由于遭到商人的强烈反对，该市场自4月15日成立以来业务寥寥无几。该市场由一名叫松本（Matsumoto）的日本人和一名叫王老強（Wang Tse-jang）的中国人管理，王任副经理。经向各同业公会查询，无人知晓其行业内有任何名为此人者。

另获悉，傀儡机关成立该市场的目的是完全控制牲畜运输。内地商人被迫通过日本船只将货物运往上海，且除非将货物送至该市场，否则不允许交付。每头牛收取10美元、每头猪2美元、每只家禽0.10美元的巨额佣金。

各牲畜同业公会坚决拒绝与牲畜市场合作。除了本地猪行同仁发表的联合宣言外，牛羊商人也反对该市场，全体牲畜商人甚至不惜全面停业。至于那些秘密加入市场的人，爱国团体已发出警告。猪商已查明加入牲畜市场者的姓名，正在 devising（策划）应对之策。

昨日，数百头猪经火车运抵上海，并被带至虹口的牲畜市场。随后，此事以每头猪支付1.10美元得以解决。市场出具了一份证书，声明已履行必要手续，武装人员应允许将猪带走。所收款项数额及负责人姓名均未提及。

猪商极为愤慨，并威胁停止向上海订购生猪。若发生这种情况，上海将出现猪肉短缺。

April 16, 1939.

"Shanghai Livestock Market" - to monopolize the livestock
trade in Shanghai
------------------------------------------------------------

On April 10, a Branch Office of a "Shanghai
Livestock Market" (上海畜牲市場) was established in
Room 127 Embankment Building, 400 North Soochow Road.
On April 12, it published two notices in the
"Eastern Times". One of the notices states that the
market will commence functioning on April 15 at a
temporary address, 52 Yochow Road and hopes that all
dealers will join the market. It mentions that a
permanent market is being built at the corner of
Chaoufoong Road and Vuh Hwa Road (O.O.L.). The
second notice states that as from April 15, the
market will be the sole agency for the transportation
and sale of all kinds of livestock and instructs pig
brokers, livestock dealers, and boatmen engaged in
livestock transportation to register with the market
between April 16 and 30.
Enquiries made at the branch office in the
Embankment Building show that it is promoted and
operated by a Japanese named Matsuhara (松原) with
a Chinese named Wong Ts-Jang (王志強), who acts as
Manager of the market. They claim to have secured
permission from the Japanese Military Authorities and
the "Reformed Government" to conduct such a market.
This person Wong was formerly a secretary in the employ
of the Pig Hong Guild (now defunct), Sih Ka Frng, Nantao.
The intention of controlling the livestock trade as a
whole from April 15 is not to be carried out meantime,
it is learned, but they will confine themselves to

1939年4月16日。

“上海牲畜市场” - 意图垄断上海牲畜贸易
------------------------------------------------------------

4月10日，“上海牲畜市场”（上海畜牲市場）的一个分办事处在北苏州路400号河滨大楼127室成立。
4月12日，它在《时报》（Eastern Times）上刊登了两则通告。其中一则通告称，市场将于4月15日在临时地址周家嘴路（Yochow Road）52号开始运作，并希望所有商人都加入市场。通告提到，一个永久性市场正在兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）和五华路（Vuh Hwa Road）（O.O.L.）转角处建造。第二则通告称，自4月15日起，该市场将成为所有种类牲畜运输和销售的唯一代理机构，并指示猪经纪人、牲畜商人以及从事牲畜运输的船夫在4月16日至30日期间向市场注册。
对河滨大楼分办事处的查询显示，该市场由一名叫松原（Matsuhara，松原）的日本人推动和运营，并由一名叫王志強（Wong Ts-Jang，王志強）的中国人担任市场经理。他们声称已获得日本军方当局和“维新政府”的许可来经营此类市场。此人王曾是南市四加坊（Sih Ka Frng，音译）猪行公会（现已解散）的秘书。
据悉，从4月15日起全面控制牲畜贸易的意图暂时不会实施，但他们将局限于

走访兆丰路（Chaoufoong）和五华路（Vuh Wa）附近，未发现任何施工迹象。

The present situation in the local pig trade
is as follows:-
    There are two markets: one, the so-called
Northern District (Settlement ) Market located at 273
Penang Road, and the other, the so-called Southern
District (French Concession) Market located at 311 Rue
Pere Proc. These two markets have a joint delivery
office in Room 205, 264 Kiangse Road and take care of
53 pig hongs.
    The Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao,
closed on the outbreak of hostilities. The pig hong
dealers are, however, more or less secretly maintaining
a "Southern & Northern District Pig Hong Traders' Joint
Office" in the residence of a lawyer named Chang
Yih ( 张翼 ), 1 Liang Jing Faung ( 卞勤坊 ), Rue
Lafayette. Mr. Chang was secretary to the now
defunct Pig Hong Guild at Sih Ka Pang, Nantao, and
a staff employee of the now defunct Bureau of Social
Affairs of the Shanghai City Government.
    Between 2.30 p.m. and 5 p.m. April 13, six
representatives of local pig hongs held a meeting in
the "Southern & Northern District Ping Hong Traders'
Joint Office", 1 Liang Jing Faung, Rue Lafayette.
Mr. Hung Wen-kiang ( 洪文江 ), Assistant Manager
of the Penang Road Pig Market, who presided, reported
that out of a total of 53 pig hongs, 47 have pledged
to refuse to join the "Bogus Livestock Market".
According to the pledge, in order to fulfil the
duties of a Chinese citizen, the person pledging
his word is requested to refuse to co-operate with
the bogus establishment and that he is willing to

本地猪业目前的状况如下：
    有两个市场：一个是所谓的北区（公共租界）市场，位于槟榔路（Penang Road）273号；另一个是所谓的南区（法租界）市场，位于神父路（Rue Pere Proc.）311号。这两个市场在江西路264号205室设有联合交货处，服务于53家猪行。
    南市四加坊（Sih Ka Pang，音译）的猪行公会在战事爆发时关闭。然而，猪行商人在一定程度上秘密维持着一个“南北区猪行联合办事处”，地点位于拉斐德路卞勤坊（Liang Jing Faung，卞勤坊）1号律师张翼（Chang Yih，张翼）的寓所内。张先生曾是南市四加坊现已解散的猪行公会的秘书，也是上海市政府社会局（现已解散）的一名职员。
    4月13日下午2:30至5:00之间，六名本地猪行代表在拉斐德路卞勤坊1号的“南北区猪行联合办事处”举行会议。主持会议的是槟榔路猪市副经理洪文江（Hung Wen-kiang，洪文江）先生，他报告说，在总共53家猪行中，有47家已承诺拒绝加入“伪牲畜市场”。根据承诺，为了履行中国公民的职责，承诺者被要求拒绝与该伪机构合作，并且他愿意

pages.en:

receive any punishment should he be found to have
broken this pledge. Discussion took place and the
following resolutions were finally reached :-
1. That a committee of seven persons including
Mr. Hung Wen-kiang (洪文江) and Mr. Chang Yih (張翼)
be formed to look after the safe custody of the
pledges.
2. That a manifesto containing the opinion of the
pig hongs to refuse to join the "Livestock Market"
be published in the Chinese press.
3. That should the "Livestock Market" insist on a
monopoly by dint of its influence, all the persons
who have pledged this word should suspend business.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / S.B. REGISTRY / No. S. B. D. 8637 A/5 / Date April 15, 1939）
Subject "Shanghai Livestock Market" - to monopolize the livestock
trade in Shanghai.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Crawford S.I.

On April 10, a Branch Office of a "Shanghai
Livestock Market" (上海市牲畜市場) was established in
Room 127 Embankment Building, 400 North Soochow Road.
On April 12, it published two notices in the
"Eastern Times". One of the notices states that the
market will commence functioning on April 15 at a
temporary address, 52 Yochow Road and hopes that all
dealers will join the market. It mentions that a
permanent market is being built at the corner of
Chaoufoong Road and Vuh Hwa Road (O.O.L.). The
second notice states that as from April 15, the
market will be the sole agency for the transportation
and sale of all kinds of livestock and instructs pig
brokers, livestock dealers, and boatmen engaged in
livestock transportation to register with the market
between April 16 and 30.
Enquiries made at the branch office in the
Embankment Building show that it is promoted and
operated by a Japanese named Matsuhara (松原 ) with
a Chinese named Wong Ts-jang (王志強 ), who acts as
Manager of the market. They claim to have secured
permission from the Japanese Military Authorities and
the "Reformed Government" to conduct such a market.
This person Wong was formerly a secretary in the employ
of the Pig Hong Guild (now defunct), Sih Ka Pang, Nantao.
The intention of controlling the livestock trade as a
whole from April 15 is not to be carried out meantime,
it is learned, but they will confine themselves to

由特别分部督察高延肯（Kao Yen-ken）撰写，由特别分部督察 C. Crawford 转呈。

4月10日，“上海牲畜市场”（上海市牲畜市場）的一个分支机构在北苏州路400号河滨大楼127室成立。
4月12日，该市场在《字林西报》（Eastern Times）上刊登了两则通告。其中一则通告称，市场将于4月15日在临时地址余姚路52号开始运作，并希望所有商贩加入该市场。通告提及，一个永久性市场正在兆丰路（Chaoufoong Road）和物华路（Vuh Hwa Road）（O.O.L.）的拐角处建设中。第二则通告称，自4月15日起，该市场将成为所有种类牲畜运输和销售的唯一代理机构，并指示猪经纪人、牲畜商贩以及从事牲畜运输的船夫于4月16日至30日期间向市场注册。
对河滨大楼分支机构的查询显示，该市场由一名叫松原（Matsuhara）的日本人和一名叫王志強（Wong Ts-jang）的中国人推动和运营，后者担任市场经理。他们声称已获得日本军方当局和“维新政府”的许可来经营此类市场。此人王曾是南市四家浜猪行公会（现已解散）的秘书。
据悉，从4月15日起全面控制牲畜贸易的意图暂时不会实施，但他们将局限于

April 14, 1939.    Morning Translation.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 14 APR. 1939）

FIG HONGS PUBLISH JOINT NOTICE

The following notice published jointly by
the Zang Zung Hong (長順行) and 46 other pig hongs
in Shanghai appears in the "Sin Wan Pao" and other
local newspapers to-day :-
    "Formerly we used to do business in Nantao, （批：Sp Br Perhaps an）
Woosung, Yangking (洋涇) and other places. We removed
into the Foreign Settlements because of the outbreak （批：shall be -）
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities on August 15, 1937. （批：before - K）
Our aim is to regulate the supply of pigs for the
requirements of the public. Since February this year, （批：present state）
a certain percentage of the tax has been donated as
monthly contribution towards the relief of refugees. （批：of pig monopoly）
This has been going on up to the present. Furthermore, （批：etc (short)）
we have always performed our obligations as citizens
of the Republic of China. （批：J. H. Sec）
    "Of late a certain organ has come into
existence and attempted by inducements and coercion to
break up the unification of the pig dealers and harm
the pig trade. We are publishing this notice for the
information of the general public and to state that
the pig hongs which have signed this notice will have
no part in any illegitimate organization nor will we
submit to coercion or oppression. We will remain firm
and as a mark of determination to observe this decision,
a declaration form in duplicate has been signed by
every one of us.
    "Lest the public should be misled by reports
prevailing locally, this notice is issued to remove
such misunderstanding."

（手写：d / R / 1374.）

    “昔日我们在南市、（批注：特别分部 或许是一个）
吴淞、洋泾（Yangking）等地经商。因1937年8月15日中日战事爆发，（批注：应为 -）
我们迁入外国租界。（批注：之前 - K）
我们的宗旨是调节生猪供应以满足公众需求。自今年二月起，（批注：现状）
我们将一定比例的税款作为月度捐款，用于难民救济。（批注：关于猪肉垄断）
此事一直持续至今。此外，（批注：等（简写））
我们始终履行作为中华民国公民的义务。（批注：J. H. Sec）
    “近来，某一机构成立，试图通过利诱和胁迫破坏猪商的团结，损害猪肉贸易。我们发布此通告以告知公众，并声明签署此通告的猪行不参与任何非法组织，也不屈服于胁迫或压迫。我们将保持坚定，为表明遵守此决定的决心，我们每人均签署了一式两份的声明书。
    “为防止公众被当地流传的报道误导，特发此通告以消除误解。”

Owing to opposition from pig dealers,
the puppet pork market has not yet been opened.
A certain Japanese hong, with the object

PLAN TO SEIZE CONTROL OF PORK BUSINESS IN SHANGHAI

A local Japanese pork dealer named Sato,
in conspiracy with certain Chinese merchants, is planning
to open a pork market with the object of seizing control
of the pork business in Shanghai. Preparations for
the formation of the pork market were commenced in July
last year. The market has been registered with the
Ministry of Industry of the "Reformed Government" and
with the Social Affairs Bureau of the Shanghai City
Government. The market has not yet been inaugurated
because pork dealers are refusing to join it.
According to information from interested
sources, the promoters of the pork market intend to
establish a market at Yangtsepoo with the assistance
of the Japanese authorities. It is understood that
after the establishment of the pork market, it will
exercise control over abattoirs and will collect taxes.

《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

图谋控制上海猪肉业计划

一名名为佐藤（Sato，音译）的本地日本猪肉商，与某些中国商人合谋，正计划开设一个猪肉市场，旨在夺取上海猪肉业的控制权。组建该猪肉市场的准备工作于去年七月开始。该市场已向“维新政府”实业部及上海市政府社会局注册。由于猪肉商拒绝加入，该市场尚未正式开业。

March 10, 1939. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

PLAN TO SEIZE CONTROL OF PORK BUSINESS IN SHANGHAI

A local Japanese pork dealer named Sato,
in conspiracy with certain Chinese merchants, is planning
to open a pork market with the object of seizing control
of the pork business in Shanghai. Preparations for
the formation of the pork market were commenced in July
last year. The market has been registered with the
Ministry of Industry of the "Reformed Government" and
with the Social Affairs Bureau of the Shanghai City
Government. The market has not yet been inaugurated
because pork dealers are refusing to join it.
According to information from interested
sources, the promoters of the pork market intend to
establish a market at Yangtsepoo with the assistance
of the Japanese authorities. It is understood that
after the establishment of the pork market, it will
exercise control over abattoirs and will collect tax.

Ta Mei Pao and other local newspapers :-
J.-P.N'S ATTEMPT TO MONOPOLIZE PIG TRADE
Owing to opposition from pig dealers,
the puppet pork market has not yet been opened.
A certain Japanese hong, with the object
of monopolizing the pork business, has prohibited the
transportation of pigs from Kompo; furthermore it has
started the purchase of pigs for the market in Shanghai.
The other day 600 pigs were brought to Shanghai by the
hong and were landed at Yangtszepoo for disposal in the
two Foreign Settlements.
The pig dealers are devising ways and means
to deal with this situation. They will not co-operate
with the puppet market.

Further to Special Branch report dated April 5,
1939, on the above subject, the 1,180 pigs which arrived
here from Singkong on April 3 on board a Japanese vessel,
which berthed at Loh Ka Ts, Poctung, and which were not
unloaded because of the collection of an additional
charge of $2 per head by the Japanese authorities, were
landed on April 5, following the Japanese authorities
agreeing to reduce the charge to $1 each pig. It is
also learned that hereafter a tax of $1 per pig will be
collected by the Japanese on arrivals from Singkong,
whether they are brought here in Japanese ships or those
of foreign concerns.

According to the pig hong owners, $8.65 is paid on
every pig brought here from Kompo, which covers freight
charges a tax of $2 paid to the Japanese at Kompo and $1
at Shanghai, and this money was paid previously by the
pig dealers at Kompo, so the pig hong owners at Shanghai
are to open negotiations with the pig dealers at Kompo
for the payment of the above mentioned tax of $1 required
by the Japanese in Shanghai.

With reference to the attached newspaper cutting
from the North China Daily News dated April 4, 1939,
stating that British steamships were prevented from
carrying pigs from Kompo to Shanghai by the Japanese
authorities, enquiries have been made and the
following information obtained:-

On April 2, 1939, when two British steamships,
namely the Christine Moller and the Whangpoo, were
about to load some 1,180 pigs at Singkong, they
were prevented from doing so by the Japanese
authorities who compelled the coolies to load the
pigs into a Japanese vessel, which arrived in Shanghai
on the night of March 3 and is now anchored at Loh
Ka Ts (陸家嘴), Pootung.

The pigs could have been unloaded yesterday
(March 4), but the Japanese Authorities are demanding
the payment of an additional charge of $2 for each
pig, and in consequence of a refusal to pay by the
dealers the pigs were not unloaded. Negotiations with
the Japanese authorities are now being carried out by
the pig hong owners concerned.

It is reported that the Japanese authorities at
Singkong will prevent the loading of pigs into
foreign vessels, should it come to their notice, but
should the pigs be already aboard the vessel they
do not interfere.
