NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,
03573
APR 4 1939

Japanese Restrain
Yangtze Delta Pigs
Armed Parties Prevent
Loading on British Boats;
Junkmen Threatened

Two British steamships, the Christine Moller and Whangpu were deprived of about 2,000 live pigs which their crews were about to receive into their holds when five or six launches bearing parties of armed Japanese prevented junks carrying the livestock from approaching the British boats anchored at Hsinkiang, the riverport gateway to Chinkiang, north Kiangsu. The Japanese diverted the junks to a Japanese vessel anchored not far away, it is alleged.

According to eye-witnesses, this happened at about 5 p.m. on Sunday when the British vessels were about to load the pigs for Shanghai. The Christine Moller had been consigned 1,000 pigs and the Whangpu about 450 but were prevented from doing so on account of the interference, which, it is stated, aimed chiefly at giving priority to Japanese shipping interests.

It is said that similar trouble occurred often lately when several Japanese merchant vessels were put on regular runs between Shanghai and Kiangsu coastal districts. Junks carrying cargo destined for third party ships were prevented from approaching them. Junkmen were forced by armed Japanese to sail their boats to Japanese vessels so that the latter might carry the cargo to Yangtzepoo.

Chinese Interpreters

In the Japanese launches are Chinese interpreters who would tell the junkmen that they would have to sail to the Japanese vessels otherwise they would be arrested. Recently, it is stated, one shot was fired by the Japanese when junkmen did not obey the order promptly. These Japanese launches cruise round daily and their interference with foreign traders may cause serious losses in future.

It is explained by one eye-witness, however, that this interference does not mean that British ships are not allowed to do business—when Japanese vessels are full foreign steamships are permitted to load cargo.

It is estimated that about 1,000 pigs were to have been carried to Shanghai in the Christine Moller which arrived here yesterday afternoon, but she did not return with empty holds, however, for she went to Lokachiao after being prevented from loading at Hsinkiang. So she carried other cargo to Shanghai as did the Whangpu, eggs, fish and other livestock.

It is feared by informed quarters that in addition to the Whangpu another Butterfield & Swire vessel, the ss. Wusueh, might have suffered the same fate. This depended on whether or not a Japanese vessel was anchored in the vicinity. The Wusueh is expected her today. The ss. Suiwo (Jardines) may also have similarly treated.

It is also learnt that about 80 Japanese soldiers are stationed at Chinkiang where barracks have been built. Curfew begins at 6 p.m., after which hour no cargo is to be transported from the district.

（手写批注：D.S. Kel R / C.K. 4/4 / O.T. Lau, Pan / Luzy）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，
03573
1939年4月4日

日本限制
长江三角洲生猪
武装人员阻止
装上英国船只；
船夫受到威胁

两艘英国轮船，“克里斯汀·莫勒”号和“黄埔”号，失去了约2,000头活猪，当时其船员正准备将这些猪接收进舱，此时五或六艘载有武装日本人的小艇阻止运载牲畜的舢板靠近停泊在江苏北部镇江通往长江的河港门户新港（Hsinkiang，音译）的英国船只。据称，日本人将这些舢板改道至不远处锚泊的一艘日本船只。

据目击者称，此事发生在周日下午5点左右，当时英国船只正准备装载运往上海的生猪。“克里斯汀·莫勒”号已被指派装载1,000头生猪，“黄埔”号约为450头，但因干扰而未能装载，据说此举主要旨在给予日本航运利益优先权。

据说最近经常发生类似的麻烦，当时几艘日本商船被投入上海与江苏沿海地区之间的定期航线。运载 destined for third party ships（原文不清，意指运往第三方船只货物）的舢板被阻止靠近它们。船夫被武装日本人强迫将船驶向日本船只，以便后者将货物运往杨树浦。

中国翻译

在日本小艇上有中国翻译，他们会告诉船夫，他们必须驶向日本船只，否则将被逮捕。据说，最近当船夫没有迅速服从命令时，日本人开了一枪。这些日本小艇每天巡航，它们对外国贸易商的干扰未来可能会造成严重损失。

然而，一位目击者解释说，这种干扰并不意味着不允许英国船只做生意——当日本船只满员时，外国轮船被允许装载货物。

据估计，“克里斯汀·莫勒”号原计划运载约1,000头生猪至上海，该船于昨天下午抵达此处，但她并未空舱返回，因为在新港被阻止装载后，她去了洛家桥（Lokachiao，音译）。因此，她和“黄埔”号一样，将其他货物如鸡蛋、鱼和其他牲畜运到了上海。

知情人士担心，除了“黄埔”号外，另一艘宝丰洋行（Butterfield & Swire）的船只“吴淞”号（ss. Wusueh，音译）可能也遭遇了同样的命运。这取决于附近是否锚泊有日本船只。“吴淞”号预计今天抵达此处。怡和洋行（Jardines）的“绥远”号（ss. Suiwo，音译）也可能受到类似对待。

另获悉，约有80名日本士兵驻扎在镇江，那里已修建了兵营。宵禁从下午6点开始，此后该区域不得运输任何货物。

（手写批注：D.S. Kel R / C.K. 4/4 / O.T. Lau, Pan / Luzy）

Subject... Restrictions by Japanese Naval Landing Party at Sinkiang

Made by Inspector Lees ........Forwarded by......... (Signature)

Sir,

    The undersigned having heard that the Japanese
Authorities are endeavouring to stop foreigner's
transporting livestock from Sinkiang, Kiangsu Province,
to Shanghai, questioned Mr. Tsok Nyau Ziang (竺鹤祥)
of the Nyeu Loong Company, 274 Avenue Edward VII, Room
41, Charterer's of the British vessel "Christine Mollar"
property of Messrs Moller's Towages Co. Ltd. Hongkong
& Shanghai Bank Building, 12 The Bund and ascertained
the following :-

    The above named vessel runs between Shanghai
and Sinkiang arriving each port every other day.

    Having no wharves at Sinkiang it is necessary
to deliver the pigs by Chinese junks from the shore to
the vessels.

    On this last visit to Sinkiang on the 4-4-39,
whilst the Junks were bringing the pigs from the shore
to the "Christine Mollar" they were intercepted by a
Japanese Naval River Boat, and were informed that they
would not be permitted to load the pigs onto a British
ship but that they could transport them by a Japanese
vessel.

    The Japanese vessel being very small could only
carry about four hundred pigs and its three junks took
about 1,000 pigs, the remaining 500 pigs were permitted
to be carried by the "Christine Mollar".

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S.P.B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 3697/S(U) 2 Date 15th April 40）
Date April 15, 1940.

Subject Interference with the arrival of oxen in the Settlement
by the Japanese.

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

At 2 p.m. April 10, forty-six oxen which
arrived at the Bund by the Italian steamer "Loo Mo"
(潞瑪) from Kiangyin, were detained by the Japanese
authorities who claimed that the importation was
unauthorized. They were subsequently taken by the
Japanese authorities to the Shanghai Livestock Market,
Hongkew. They were released on April 12 and removed
to C.M.F. Abattoir, Boulevard de Montigny, after
negotiations by the consignees.

The transportation of oxen from Kiangyin
has hitherto been carried out by the s.s. "Loo An"
of the Han Wen Co.(漢文洋行), Canton Road. Owing
to a falling off in the number transported each trip,
the owners have recently demanded an increase in
freight charges, with the result that the dealers
entrusted the transportation of oxen to another
steamer, the s.s. "Loo Mo". It is reported that
owners of the former vessel reported the arrival on
April 10 to the Japanese authorities who had thus
effected the detention as above mentioned.

Kiangyin is the only source of supply of
oxen direct to the Settlement due to the absence of
Japanese troops there, but a decrease in the arrivals
has been noted recently. The decrease, it is reported,
is partly due to interference by the guerillas in the
surrounding areas and the fact that the farmers require
the services of oxen in plowing their fields during
the present season.

主题 日本人干扰牛只进入租界。

由 特别调查员 施子良（Sih Tse-liang）制作 转交者 督察长 克劳福德（Crawford）

4月10日下午2时，四十六头牛由意大利轮船“潞瑪”号（Loo Mo）从江阴运抵外滩，被日本当局扣留，理由是进口未经批准。随后，这些牛被日本当局带至虹口上海牲畜市场。经收货人交涉，它们于4月12日被释放，并移至蒙蒂尼路（Boulevard de Montigny）的公共租界屠宰场（C.M.F. Abattoir）。

此前，从江阴运输牛只一直由汉文洋行（Han Wen Co.）广东路的“潞安”号（Loo An）轮船承担。由于每趟运输数量减少，船主最近要求增加运费，导致经销商将牛只运输委托给另一艘轮船“潞瑪”号。据报，前一艘船的船主向日本当局报告了4月10日的抵达情况，日本当局因此实施了上述扣留。

由于江阴没有日军驻扎，它是直接向租界供应牛只的唯一来源，但最近注意到抵达数量有所减少。据报道，减少的部分原因是周边地区游击队的干扰，以及当前季节农民需要牛只耕种田地。

Subject......Oxen from Kiangyin - Supply disrupted.

Made by..C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang.........Forwarded by.........Supt....J. Mason

Copy sent
to Mr. Burley

Until recently, Kiangyin, due to the
absence of Japanese troops, formed the principal
source of supply of oxen in the local foreign
controlled areas (direct to the area south of
the Creek). The foreign owned s.s. "Hai Kong"
plied between Kiangyin and Shanghai at an
interval of five days, and usually brought
several score of oxen to Shanghai on each voyage.
This source of supply has now been
disrupted owing to the presence of Japanese
troops in Kiangyin, thereby preventing the
export of oxen from that district. Consequently
the s.s. "Loo An" (安) which has replaced
the s.s. "Hai Kong" on the Kiangyin-Shanghai
run, arrived at the Bund on March 14, 1940,
without any cattle on board. It is not known
whether the presence of Japanese troops at
Kiangyin is temporary or otherwise.
The arrival of oxen from other places
destined for the Shanghai Livestock Market,
Hongkew, as well as the supply of carcasses from
this Market to the area south of the Creek is
continuing as usual.

Subject. Arrival of oxen in Shanghai and the local supply of beef.

Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford.

A total of 128 oxen arrived in Shanghai on
February 17, 1940 on the foreign-owned s.s. "Hai Kong"
( 海 康 ). The s.s. "Hai Kong" takes five days
to complete each voyage between Kiangyin which place
due to the absence of Japanese troops, forms the chief
source of supply of oxen in the local foreign controlled
areas, and Shanghai, unloading being done on The Bund.

It is learned that apart from those arriving
from Kiangyin by boat, oxen from Kintan, Chinkiang,
Wutsin etc. have been brought here via the Shanghai-
Nanking Railway. They were taken, however, to the
Shanghai Livestock Market on arrival in Shanghai.

Japanese-owned steamers only are permitted
by the Japanese Military Authorities to transport
oxen from ports in Kompo; arrivals from those places
are without exception destined for the Shanghai
Livestock Market and subsequently slaughtered in the
Municipal Abattoir, Sawgin Road.

Carcasses from the Municipal Abattoir are
also on sale in areas south of the Soochow Creek and (unintelligible)
the ruling market price for beef is 80 cents per lb.

No information on the present stock of oxen
can be obtained with any degree of accuracy but it is
held probable that arrivals from the interior average
~ 100 daily.

主题. 牛只抵达上海及本地牛肉供应。

制作人. 特别调查员 施子良（Sih Tse-liang）。 转交者. 督察长 克劳福德（Crawford）。

1940年2月17日，共有128头牛由外商所有的“海康”号（Hai Kong）轮船抵达上海。“海康”号完成江阴（该地因无日军驻扎，构成当地外侨控制区牛只供应的主要来源）与上海之间的每次航行需五天时间，卸货在外滩进行。

据悉，除了由船运从江阴抵达的牛只外，来自金坛、镇江、武进等地的牛只已通过沪宁铁路运抵此处。然而，它们在抵达上海后被带往上海牲畜市场。

日本军事当局仅允许日资轮船从镇江（Kompo，音译，疑指镇江或相关港口群）各港口运输牛只；从这些地方抵达的牛只无一例外地 destined for（目的地为）上海牲畜市场，随后在萨金路（Sawgin Road，音译，疑指宰牲场路或类似地点）的公共租界屠宰场屠宰。

公共租界屠宰场的胴体也在苏州河以南地区和（原文不清）出售，牛肉的市场通行价格为每磅80美分。

无法获得关于当前牛只存量的任何准确信息，但据信来自内地的抵达量平均每天约100头。

FILE
C 7/8

The temporary offices of the "Shanghai
Livestock Market" at 269 Broadway, and 47-51 and 52
Yochow Road, were on August 23 removed to the newly
constructed site of the market on Fuhwa Road, off
Chaoufoong Road, O.O.L.

The market commenced enforcing a monopoly
on cattle, sheep and fowl on August 1. The market
regulations are that all cattle will for the time
being be sent and slaughtered at Sawgin Road S.M.C.
Abattoir and will include cattle destined for the
French Concession, but the hides must be sold to
the Japanese Military Authorities at a price which
will be fixed later. The hides of the cattle
slaughtered already are temporarily being stored by
the market. It is reported that the market intends
monopolizing the slaughtering of cattle in its new
site on Fuhwa Road, when adequate premises have been
constructed.

The market charges the dealers $2.00 for
each cow, $0.70 for each pig, $0.20 for each sheep
and 2% of the cost price of fowl as a market tax.

Date... July ... 27, ... 1939.

Subject... Detention of Cattle by the Japanese Special Service Section.

Made by........................................ Forwarded by........................................

Information has been received to the effect
that on July 22, 1939, some 90 head of oxen which
were destined for Shanghai being transported by
the Shanghai-Nanking Railway from Perniu (奔牛)
were detained by members of the Japanese Special
Service Section at the Markham Road Junction on
the pretext that the transportation permit was not
in order.    A further 200 head were also detained
the next three days on the same pretext. Negotiations
were subsequently entered into between the holders
of the livestock and the authorities issuing the
permit and an agreement was finally reached wherein
the holders promised to have their oxen slaughtered
at the Sawgin Road Abattoir and the skins sold to the
Japanese.

It is learned that although the "Shanghai
Livestock Market", Hongkew, has made arrangements
for the monopoly of the sale of cattle from August
1, 1939, it is improbable that they will be in a
position to carry out this measure as the construction
work for the bullock pens has not as yet commenced.

REPORT
Date October 18, 19 38.

Subject Hwa Mei Chen Pao reports Japanese stop transportation of cows
into Foreign Settlements - incorrect.

Made by D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by (签名)

With reference to the attached translation of an extract
from Hwa Mei Chen Pao, October 7th issue, enquiries made by
the Special Branch reveals that the report is incorrect.

Since the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in
August, 1937, Shanghai has been supplied with cows chiefly
from Kompo and the northern provinces, and the transportation
has never been interfered with.

The western suburbs of Shanghai which constitute the
source of a small part of the supply of the livestock for
this city, is at present practically under the monopoly of
the "Ruh Shing 合興宰牲公司 Slaughter House," situated at 56 Lao Wen Dong
Loong (老混堂弄), off Jessfield Road, O.O.L. This establish-
ment is in possession of a special pass issued by the Japanese
Military by which it is entitled to the privilege of transport-
ing cows from the western suburbs to Shanghai, either by land
or by water, at a duty of $5.00 per head, whereas other cow
dealers are charged for each cow, $10.00 at the place from
where it is exported and another $10.00 at its destination.

This Slaughter House is under the management of Pan Sao
Mei (潘少梅), a former local newspaper reporter, residing at
No.11, Mei Tsung Terrace, off Jessfield Road, O.O.L., and
Zung Foh Shing (陳福興), alias Zung Vung Yao (陳文耀), a
cow dealer, residing at No.4 Ting Nyih Li (鼎業里), off Brenan
Road, O.O.L.. The former is reported to be on very intimate
terms with one Kitaoka (Japanese), Director of the Shanghai
City Government in the Jessfield Area, and a number of Chinese
staff employees of that organ.

For each cow slaughtered this Slaughter House pays a tax
of $1.00 to the Shanghai City Government.

D.C. (Special Branch)
Liao Chungchieh
D.S.I.

主题：《华美晨报》报道日本阻止牛只运入外国租界——不实。

制作人：副督察廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien） 转呈人：(签名)

关于附译的10月7日《华美晨报》摘录，经特务科查询，该报道不实。

自1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发以来，上海的牛只供应主要来自江浦（Kompo）及北方省份，运输从未受到干扰。

构成本市部分牲畜来源的上海西郊，目前实际上由位于越界筑路区域极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）旁老混堂弄56号的“合興宰牲公司”（Ruh Shing Slaughter House）垄断。该机构持有日本军方颁发的特别通行证，享有将牛只从西郊经陆路或水路运入上海的特权，每头牛税费为5.00元；而其他牛商则在出口地和目的地各被收取每头牛10.00元的费用。

该屠宰场由前本地报纸记者潘少梅（Pan Sao Mei）管理，其住址为越界筑路区域极司菲尔路旁美宗里11号；另一管理者为牛商陈福兴（Zung Foh Shing），别名陈文耀（Zung Vung Yao），其住址为越界筑路区域勃伦南路（Brenan Road）旁鼎业里4号。据报，前者与日本籍的极司菲尔地区上海市政府主任北冈（Kitaoka）及其机构中的多名中国职员关系密切。

该屠宰场每屠宰一头牛，需向上海市政府缴纳1.00元税款。

副总监（特务科）
廖仲坚
副督察

Further report re Slaughter House, Lane 1050/49,
Lane 1050/50 North Chengtu Road.

At 12 noon 18/5/59, a telephone message was received
from C.P.C. 3233, on duty at the Soo Sih (蘇錫) Slaugh-
ter House, Lane 1050/50 North Chengtu Road, to the effect
that a bomb had been found near the above slaughter house

D.I. Boddy, C.P.C. 333 and the undersigned attended
immediately and found an unexploded handgrenade of the
"potato masher " type - partly covered by a cloth apron
similar to those worn by foodshop coolies - lying in
Lane 1019, North Chengtu Road, opposite House No. 48,
and immediately behind the Soo Sih Slaughter House
premises.

（批：C/N 20/5/59）

Enquiries at the scene reveal that at about 12 noon
C.P.C.2239,
18/5/59, whilst patrolling Lane 1050, North Chengtu Road,
near the above slaughter house, when he noticed a crowd
congregating at the rear. On approaching he discovered
the handgrenade.

Extensive enquiries were conducted in the vicinity,
but it could not be ascertained at what time or by whom
the missile was conveyed to the scene.

It is presumed that the placing of the handgrenade
is a further act of intimidation directed against the
slaughter houses.

ing character (四+乙) (42), and on a piece of torn

第333号华籍巡捕 Boddy 副督察和本报告人立即赶赴现场，发现在成都北路1019弄，48号房屋对面，紧靠苏锡屠宰场后方的巷子里，有一枚未爆炸的“马铃薯捣碎器”式手榴弹，部分被一块类似食品店苦力所穿的布围裙遮盖。

（批：C/N 1959年5月20日）

经现场调查得知，1959年5月18日中午12时许，第2239号华籍巡捕在上述屠宰场附近的成都北路1050弄巡逻时，注意到后方聚集了一群人。上前查看时发现了这枚手榴弹。

Further report re slaughter-houses, 1050/48.

At 6.40p.m. 17-5-39, Inspt. Macfarlane received a telephone message from D.S.I. Kobiyashi, informing that he had received information that intimidation was being carried on at the Sing Nyung Hai (新寧海) and Soo Sin (苏锡) Slaughter Houses, Lane 1050/48-50, North Chengtu Road.

The undersigned communicated with D.S.I. Kobiyashi, who stated that he would bring his informant to the Station immediately. A visit was meanwhile paid to the slaughter houses and no evidence of intimidation was found and no untoward incident reported. Two C.P.Cs were on duty there and the guards were doubled from 7p.m. onwards.

At about 7.30p.m. D.S.I. Kobiyashi brought to the Station Mr. Chejiro Takasu, representative of the Shanghai Poultry Market, Offices 269 Broadway, Branch Office 400 N/Soochow Road, c/o Embankment Building, with a market place situated at 52 Yochow Road. He explained that his concern obtained pigs from the country and sold and delivered to certain Chinese purchasers residing South of the Creek. He did not disclose the identities of these buyers but stated that several of them were share-holders in the slaughter-houses in question; and that he had made recent arrangements for slaughtering

关于屠宰场，成都北路1050弄48号、

1939年5月17日下午6时40分，Macfarlane 督察接到副督察长 Kobiyashi 的电话留言，告知他收到消息，称在成都北路1050弄48-50号的新宁海（Sing Nyung Hai）和苏锡（Soo Sin）屠宰场正在进行恐吓活动。

本报告人与副督察长 Kobiyashi 取得联系，他表示将立即将其线人带至巡捕房。与此同时，有人前往屠宰场查看，未发现任何恐吓证据，也未报告发生任何意外事件。两名华籍巡捕在那里执勤，并从晚上7点起加倍了警卫力量。

晚上7时30分左右，副督察长 Kobiyashi 将上海家禽市场代表高须治次郎（Chejiro Takasu）先生带到巡捕房，该市场办事处位于百老汇路269号，分办事处位于北苏州路400号外滩大厦转交，交易场所位于宜昌路52号。他解释说，他的商号从乡下收购生猪，并出售交付给居住在苏州河以南的某些中国买家。他没有透露这些买家的身份，但指出其中几人是涉案屠宰场的股东；并且他最近已安排将

(榮福昌), manager of the Soo Sih.
At 3p.m. even date, a shipment of pigs were dis-
patched by the Shanghai Poultry Market to both slaughter
houses, 317 to the Sing Nyung Hai and 59 to the Soo Sih
for slaughtering. Later, he was informed by his Chinese
transportation company manager (particulars unknown)
that the pigs had been admitted but that he had been
informed by inmates that they would not be killed, but
no explanation was given.
Mr. Takasu stated he telephoned both slaughter
houses at about 5.30p.m. even date, and received the
reply from unknown persons therein that no slaughtering
could be carried out as both establishments had received
threats by certain Chinese and were afraid to operate.
Mr. Takasu, D.S.I, Kobiyashi and the undersigned
visited both slaughter houses and interviewed Wong Kyi
Shee (王继基), the assistant manager of the Sing Nyung
Hai and Zang Pau Tsang (盛宝昌), accountant of the Soo
Sih. Both denied all knowledge of the alleged threats
or telephone call, and that if both operated together
and that Police protection was maintained, they would
certainly slaughter and that they had already informed
Inspt. Ribbens that they were operating even date.
The office staff all denied any knowledge of the

高须先生称，他在当天下午5时30分左右致电两家屠宰场，接到里面不知名人士的回复，称由于两家机构都收到了某些中国人的威胁，不敢运营，因此无法进行屠宰。
高须先生、副督察长 Kobiyashi 和本报告人走访了两家屠宰场，并面谈了新宁海副经理王继基（Wong Kyi Shee）和苏锡会计盛宝昌（Zang Pau Tsang）。两人都否认知晓所谓的威胁或电话，并表示如果双方共同运营且维持警方保护，他们肯定会进行屠宰，而且他们已告知 Ribbens 督察他们在当天仍在运营。

At 10a.m. 10-5-39, a telephone message was
received from Mr. J.J. Carney, Chief Inspector,
Public Health Department, to the effect that letters
of a threatening nature had been received at the
Sing Hyung Hai (新甯海) Slaughter House, Lane
1050/48 North Chengtu Road.

Enquiries by C.D.C. 54 and the undersigned
revealed that at about 12noon. 9-5-39, a letter of
a threatening nature had been delivered by post
to Yu Ching Foo (虞金甫), manager, Sing Hyung Hai
Slaughter House, Lane 1050/48 North Chengtu Road.

The contents of the letter are as follows:-

Mr. Yu Ching Foo,
Information has been received to the
effect that a live-stock market is being
organised in Hongkew District to monopolise
the pig business. Two slaughter houses named
Soo Sin and Hyung Hai are co-operating with
them.
More than two years have passed since
the invasion of the Japanese. All the people
have become angry but those traitors, however,
are willing to assist them establish the
market. Those traitors should be severely
punished.
During the time we were about to abolish
the above market, unexpectedly you have
rendered them much service instead of joining

虞金甫先生，

Mr. Yu Ching Foo,
Information has been received to the effect that a live-stock market is being organised in Hongkew District to monopolise the pig business. Two slaughter houses named Soo Sih and Nyung Hai are co-operating with them.
More than two years have passed since the invasion of the Japanese. All the people have become angry but those traitors, however, are willing to assist them establish the market. Those traitors should be severely punished.
During the time we were about to abolish the above market, unexpectedly you have rendered them much service instead of joining the strike which has been staged in the International Settlement during the passed three or four days with a view to indicating that we are going to hold out to the end despite all sacrifices.
Please be sympathetic and join the strike, otherwise serious action will be taken against you.

Woo Yuin Ching.
Changchow                                      Clerk Tsao Hsu Fan.
Sinza St'n           7-5-39.                   translated
                                               --------  Clerk Tsao Hsu Fan.

    My name is Woo Yuin Ching, age 42 years, and a native of
Changchow. I am living at House 168, Lane 51, Stone Bridge
Road. On 1-5-39, the Market for Animals was formally organized
in Hongkew. Due to the fact that pigs from other sources were
not sufficient to distribute among the pork shops in Shanghai,
the shop masters tried to purchase pigs from Hongkew. On
4th and 5th of May 1939, pigs were transported from Hongkew,
but the Sing Nyung Hai and Soo Sin Slaughter Houses refused
to accept them and returned them. As the various slaughterers and
shop masters had no other means to carry on their business,
they proceeded to the home of Assistant Manager of Sing Nyung
Hai Slaughter House named Wong on Tseepang Road, for assistance.
I, being the man responsible for the transportation of pigs
from Hongkew, went with them. During the interview, Mr. Wong
stated that should Soo Sin Slaughter House accept any pigs that
came from Hongkew, they will do the same. At 4p.m. on 6-5-39,
61 pigs were transported from Hongkew and these the Soo Sin
Slaughter House accepted. Therefore, at 6p.m. same date, when
135 pigs again arrived, they were driven into the Sing Nyung
Hai Slaughter House, but the accountant named Yu refused to
admit them. A quarrel then started between this accountant
and a number of slaughterers and shop masters. At 8p.m. I
went there to take up the matter with the accountant. We then
had a quarrel, but I have never assaulted him or acted in a threa-
tening manner.

                                        Signed: Woo Yuin Ching.
pages.zh:
胡云卿。
常州                                      职员 曹旭藩。
静安寺警署           1939年5月7日。       翻译
                                               -------- 职员 曹旭藩。

    我叫胡云卿，现年42岁，常州人。我住在石桥路51弄168号。1939年5月1日，虹口牲畜市场正式成立。由于其他来源的生猪不足以供应上海的猪肉店，店主们试图从虹口购买生猪。1939年5月4日和5日，生猪从虹口运出，但新亭海和五锡屠宰场拒绝接收并将其退回。由于各屠户和店主没有其他办法维持生意，他们前往芝罘路新亭海屠宰场副经理黄先生家中寻求帮助。
    我作为负责从虹口运输生猪的人，随同他们前往。在会谈中，黄先生表示，如果五锡屠宰场接受任何来自虹口的生猪，他们也会这样做。1939年5月6日下午4点，61头生猪从虹口运出，五锡屠宰场予以接收。因此，同日晚上6点，当135头生猪再次到达时，它们被赶进新亭海屠宰场，但名为余的会计拒绝让它们进入。随后，这名会计与数名屠户和店主发生了争吵。晚上8点，我去那里与会计交涉此事。我们随后发生了争吵，但我从未殴打他或以威胁方式行事。

                                        签名：胡云卿。

1.

Re anonymous telephone message received by the
Soo Sih Slaughter House, Lane 1050/50 N/Chengtu Rd.

At 1p.m. 6-5-39, Mr. J.J. Carney, Chief Inspector,
Public Health Department, brought to Station the attached
report which he had received from Inspector Ribbins,
attached to the Sing Nyung Hai (新章海) Slaughter House,
Lane 1050/48 North Chengtu Road.

At 1a.m. 7-5-39, a visit was paid to the above slaughter
house and Yu Kung Foh (虞根福), accountant, Sing Nyung
Hai Slaughter House and Zang Pau Tsang (常宝昌), account-
ant, Soo Sih Slaughter House, were brought to Station for
enquiries.

Enquiries reveal that on the 5-5-39 the above slaughter
houses were ordered by the Shanghai Pig Guild (上海鮮肉公會),
French Concession, not to accept any pigs from Hongkew.

Between 3p.m. and 4p.m. 5-5-39, approximately 70 pigs
arrived from Hongkew to be slaughtered at the Sing Nyung
Hai Slaughter House. Admittance was refused and they were
left in the alleyway for the night.

At about 5a.m. 6-5-39, only 6 pigs remained, the
remainder having been taken away by their respective
owners and 3 of the above mentioned 6 pigs had already
been slaughtered without permission.

Kung Foh immediately informed Inspector Ribbins that
they (the management) refused to pay the inspection fee
but the matter was eventually settled and the pigs
disposed of.

1.

关于成都北路1050弄50号五锡屠宰场收到的匿名电话留言一事。

1939年5月6日下午1点，公共卫生处总督察 J.J. Carney 先生将附后的报告带到警署，该报告是他从派驻成都北路1050弄48号新章海（Sing Nyung Hai）屠宰场的 Ribbins 督察那里收到的。

1939年5月7日凌晨1点，走访了上述屠宰场，并将新章海屠宰场会计虞根福（Yu Kung Foh）和五锡屠宰场会计常宝昌（Zang Pau Tsang）带到警署进行问询。

问询显示，1939年5月5日，上述屠宰场接到法租界上海鲜肉公会的命令，不得接收任何来自虹口的生猪。

1939年5月5日下午3点至4点之间，约70头生猪从虹口运抵新章海屠宰场准备屠宰。入场被拒，它们被留在巷子里过夜。

1939年5月6日凌晨5点左右，仅剩6头生猪，其余已被各自的主人带走，上述6头中的3头已在未经许可的情况下被屠宰。

Kung Foh 立即通知 Ribbins 督察，他们（管理层）拒绝支付检验费，但该事最终得以解决，生猪也被处理。

1 (Sheet 2)

At about 8a.m. 6-5-39, a loafer named Woo Han Yuen
(吳漢源); alias Ya Kan Hwo (夜開花), (believed to be
a conditionally released kidnapper) called on Kung Foh
and informed him that pigs would arrive that day from
Hongkew and they must be accepted and slaughtered.

Between 4p.m. and 5p.m. 6-5-39, 128 pigs arrived from
Hongkew. Admittance was refused but a little later when
pigs owned by another party were being accepted, all the
above number were driven in and slaughtering began.

At about 8p.m. 6-5-39, Kung Foh sent for Woo Han Yuen
for an explanation. A quarrel arose, during which
the latter assaulted the former who was prevented from
informing the Police.

Pigs arriving from Hongkew have also been driven into
the Soo Sih Slaughter House against instructions of
the management.

Since 1-5-39, the Soo Sih Slaughter House has received
three anonymous telephone calls warning them that if
pigs from Hongkew were slaughtered they would receive
a bomb. The last message was received at 8p.m. 6-5-39.
The Sing Nyung Hai Slaughter House has not received any
such warnings.

Two C.P.Cs. have temporarily been posted at the above
location pending further arrangements.

The attached letter and report forwarded to Head-
quarters for information.

1939年5月6日上午8点左右，一名名为吴汉源（Woo Han Yuen）、别名夜开花（Ya Kan Hwo）的无业游民（据信是一名有条件释放的绑匪）拜访了 Kung Foh，并告知他当天将有生猪从虹口运来，必须接收并屠宰。

1939年5月6日下午4点至5点之间，128头生猪从虹口运抵。入场被拒，但稍后当另一方的生猪被接收时，上述所有生猪都被赶入，屠宰开始。

1939年5月6日晚上8点左右，Kung Foh 叫来吴汉源要求解释。发生争吵，期间后者袭击了前者，后者阻止前者报警。

来自虹口的生猪也被违反管理层指令赶入五锡屠宰场。

自1939年5月1日以来，五锡屠宰场已接到三次匿名电话警告，称如果屠宰来自虹口的生猪，他们将收到炸弹。最后一条消息是在1939年5月6日晚上8点收到的。新章海屠宰场未收到此类警告。

两名中国巡捕已暂时派驻在上述地点，等待进一步安排。

At 7.59 p.m. 22/4/39, C.P.C. 1556 telephoned
to the station (Street Tel. Box 10) reporting
that a hand-grenade had been thrown into a shop
on the corner of Yates Road and Weihaiwei Road.

The undersigned and C.D.C. 26 immediately
attended and from enquiries ascertained the
following.

At about 7.50 p.m. 22/4/39 a male Chinese,
as described on Sheet 1, entered the Loh Koh Kyi
(陸稿薦) Pork Shop, 143 Yates Road, situated on
the South-West corner of Yates Road and Weihaiwei
Road, and placed a letter face down upon the
counter then left the shop. Koh Tsung Yoong
(郭崇榮) 49, Ningpo, A/shop Manager, 420 Rue
Amiral Bayle picked up the letter and saw that it
same was addressed to one Wong Miau Sung (黃妙生)
and as he was examining the letter, a hand-grenade
which failed to explode, was thrown into the
shop and struck an apprentice Wong Kwei Sung
(王貴生) 17, Poetung, S/apprentice on the head

1939年4月22日晚上7:59，巡长1556号通过电话向捕房报案（街头电话亭10号），称有一枚手榴弹被扔进耶茨路与威海卫路拐角处的一家商店。

署名者及刑事侦缉科26号立即赶赴现场，经查询查明以下情况。

1939年4月22日晚上7:50左右，一名如第1页所述的中国男子进入位于耶茨路与威海卫路西南角的耶茨路143号陆稿荐（Loh Koh Kyi）猪肉店，将一封信正面朝下放在柜台上，随即离开店铺。店员经理郭崇荣（Koh Tsung Yoong），49岁，宁波人，住址法租界贝勒路（Rue Amiral Bayle）420号，捡起信件，发现信是写给黄妙生（Wong Miau Sung）的，就在他查看信件时，一枚未爆炸的手榴弹被扔进店内，击中学徒王贵生（Wong Kwei Sung），17岁，宝同人，见习学徒的头部，致其前额轻微割伤，随后手榴弹落在店地板上。店员经理立即召唤在距店铺不到10码的耶茨路威海卫路路口执行交通任务的巡长1556号，后者在了解情况后通知了捕房。

Translation

Information has been received to the effect that
you, a bad element in the pig business, have assisted
the enemy in the organisation of a live-stock market
in the Nanking Area, thereby monopolising the live-stock
from various parts and making great profits in so doing.
Such action indeed affects the livelihood of
Shanghai citizens to a great extent.
We hereby give you a severe warning first and as
a message do not repeat, we will take more drastic
action against you.

Patriotic Anti-Enemy
25/6/38.

(萬慎) Hong, these premises being located in
Lane 119 Chekiang Road (East side) about 20 yards
North of Canton Road.

From a small apprentice named Ying An Tuh
(尹安度) employed in the above Hong it was ascer-
tained that at about 8 p.m. 15-4-39 a male Chinese,
description unobtainable, knocked upon the front
door of the hong, and as same was locked shouted
for same to be opened.

His request was refused by the above named
assistant who asked whom he wished to see and in
reply, the unknown male Chinese stated that he
wished to speak to one named Lee Tsung Zai (李振才)
the manager of the said Hong.

Lee Tsung Zai being absent at this time, the
above mentioned apprentice refused his admittance &
informed the enquirer that the manager was absent.

Ascertaining this fact, the unknown male
Chinese proceeded to a small open window located on
the ground floor of these premises, but guarded by

接到此报告后，下述考克斯（Cox）警长和 C.D.F. 274 前往事发地点，经后续查询，查明以下事实。

本案案发地点为万慎（Wan Zung）鸿（Hong，指商号/钱庄等），该处所位于浙江路（东侧）119弄，广东路以北约20码处。

据受雇于上述商号的一名名叫尹安度（Ying An Tuh）的小学徒称，1939年4月15日晚上8点左右，一名体貌特征不详的中国男子敲响了商号的前门，因门锁着，便大喊要求开门。

上述助理拒绝了他的请求，询问他想见谁，该不明身份的中国男子回答说他想与该商号经理李振才（Lee Tsung Zai）谈话。

由于李振才当时不在，上述学徒拒绝其入内，并告知询问者经理不在。

得知这一情况后，该不明身份的中国男子走到该处所底层的一个小敞窗前，但该窗装有

An examination of the hand grenade, by detectives
showed same to be very old and in an exceptionally
rusty condition, it, in all probability having just
recently been dug up.

The two bullets are .45 Calibre.

A translation of the letter left behind by the
absconded male Chinese is appended herewith, same being
self-explanatory.

"Mr. Lee Tseng Zai,
Hearing that you are very prosperous in your
business during the present critical situation any one
would think that you are quite satisfied. However recently
you firmly suggested in the Pig Owners Association that
the pigs Market be removed to Hongkew District under
enemy's shelter for the purpose of more profit. Are you
willing to such a stupid thing just for gain? We special-
ly write you this letter as a warning for it is our duty
to do so. Should you refuse our advice a final way will
be adopted.

The informant when further questioned by detec-
tives stated that to the best of his knowledge, the
manager of this hong has received no letters of a
threatening nature, neither has he on behalf of his
masters attempted to remove his business to Hongkew
as is alleged in the attached letter, an advertisement
to this effect having appeared in recent issues of
the Sin Wen Pao etc.

From the fact that no attempt was made to throw
the grenade it seems obvious that this is an attempt
by some unknown person/s to intimidate the complainant
company to refrain from registering with a New Pig
Salesman's Combine at present being formed in Hongkew.

Further enquiries were made in the vicinity of
this offence but no useful information could be
obtained.

The hand grenade is at present detained at this
Station in a bucket of water pending disposal, whilst
the two bullets will be taken to the Arms Identifi-
cation Section for examination on the 17-4-39.

April 19, 1939. Afternoon Translation

STRANGE ADVERTISEMENTS

The following notice published by one
Lee Tseng-zai (李振才) appears in the advertisement
columns of the "Sin Wan Pao" and other local newspapers
to-day :-

To ..........
Your letters and articles have been
received and in reply I have to inform you that I am a
person who knows his duty quite well and that all my
actions are always in conformity with what I have said.
Moreover, my position is quite known to the public.
If your letter was sent to me with good intentions, then
there is nothing further to be said; if otherwise,
then I cannot bear the defamation brought upon me by
misleading reports.
I hereby publish this notice as a reply
to your letter.

The following notice published jointly
by Chang Yung-chia (張雲佳) and Lu Ho-sen (呂和生)
appears in the "Sin Wan Pao" and other local newspapers
to-day :-

To ..........
Your letters have been noted and in reply
we have to inform you that we used to undertake the
transportation of pigs. In fact, we have been
undertaking this work prior to the outbreak of hostilities
on August 13, 1937, when the pig hongs were mostly
located in Nantao and Woosung. After the outbreak of
hostilities, all the pig hongs were removed to Rue du
Pere Froc, French Concession, and they have since
established a Pig Transportation Market, and we have
continued to undertake the transportation of pigs for
it. We have refused to undertake the transportation
of pigs on behalf of any other party.
We hereby publish this notice as a reply
to your letter.

Cost of Living of
Foreigner T.S.J.N
19/11/40.
Analysis Contained in
"Municipal Gazette";
Large Increase Shown

An interim report on foreign cost
of living with provisional index
figures is published today by the
Shanghai Municipal Council in a
special issue of the "Municipal
Gazette," which accompanies today's
issue of the "North-China Daily
News." The study is the work of
Prof. T. Y. Tsha, statistician attached
to the Industrial Section. The ex-
cellent co-operation of families who
have kept expenditure records has
made possible the compilation of the
index figures.

The report contains indices for
American, British, Russian and other
national groups, together with a pro-
visional consolidated foreign index.
These separate indices were compiled
to meet the view that "there is no
single foreign cost of living" in
Shanghai. Indices are based on the
records of the first three months of
the study. October-December, 1939,
and figures showing relative living
costs for eight months from October,
1939, to May, 1940, are included. It
is shown that there has been a con-
tinuous rise in these months. A con-
solidated foreign index figure repre-
sented by 100 in October, 1939, has
risen to 149.45 by May, 1940. The
foreign cost of living has, therefore,
risen by 49.45 per cent. since October,
1939.

The interim report is presented be-
cause of public concern with rising
living costs. It is stressed, however,
that the study is only in its initial
stages. It is vital that all present co-
operating families should continue to
record their expenditures till one
complete year is over. It is em-
phasized that the success of the study
depends on these families, to whom
the public is greatly indebted.

The statistician has not hesitated,
to meet public needs, to undertake
twice the great number of calcula-
tions involved, once now in the pro-
duction of the provisional indices, to
be repeated again later at the close
of the twelve months of record
keeping.

外籍人士 T.S.J.N 的生活费用
1940年11月19日。
《市政公报》所载分析；
显示大幅上涨

上海公共租界工部局在今日随《字林西报》附发的《市政公报》特刊中，发布了一份关于外籍人士生活费用的临时报告，其中包含暂定指数数据。该项研究由工业科统计员查士雅（T. Y. Tsha）教授完成。得益于那些保持支出记录的家庭的出色合作，指数数据的编制得以实现。

该报告包含美国、英国、俄罗斯及其他国籍群体的指数，以及一个暂定的外籍人士综合指数。编制这些单独指数是为了符合这样一种观点，即上海“不存在单一的外籍人士生活费用标准”。指数基于研究前三个月的记录，即1939年10月至12月，并包含了显示1939年10月至1940年5月这八个月期间相对生活费用的数据。数据显示，在这几个月中生活费用持续上升。以1939年10月为100的外籍人士综合指数，到1940年5月已升至149.45。因此，自1939年10月以来，外籍人士的生活费用上涨了49.45%。

鉴于公众对生活费用上涨的关注，现提交这份临时报告。然而，报告强调，该研究仅处于初始阶段。所有目前参与合作的家庭继续记录其支出直至满一年，这一点至关重要。报告强调，这项研究的成功取决于这些家庭，公众对他们深表感激。

为满足公众需求，这位统计员毫不犹豫地承担了两倍于所需的庞大计算工作量：一次是现在编制暂定指数，另一次将在十二个月的记录期结束时再次进行。

MAINICHI

UNNECESSARY ANXIETY OVER SHORTAGE OF LIVESTOCK:
SINO-JAPANESE LIVESTOCK GUILD ACTIVE

A livestock guild known as the
Shanghai Livestock Guild has been formed by 18 Japanese and 18
Chinese. The business of the guild is making progress
notwithstanding the excitement on the south side of the creek
over a shortage of pigs. Acting on instructions from the
Asia Development Board and the Military authorities, the
guild will regulate the entire supply of livestock such as
cows, pigs, goats, ducks etc for Shanghai. Thus the guild
will handle the 72,000 cows and 1,200,000 pigs which are required
by Shanghai every year. The guild has already purchased a
piece of land measuring about 18,000 tsubo( one tsubo equals
to 4 square yards) on Tungchow Road for the erection of a
stockyard. When the guild has become a part of the
"Reformed Government" it will supply livestock to Nanking,
Hankow and Shanghai, in fact , to the whole of Central China.

（批：G.1）
（印：CITY COMMISSIONER ... 17 MAY 1939 ...）

A movement to boycott the Shanghai
Livestock Guild is reported to have been started by about 2,000
Chinese shops on the south side of the creek. This is an
anti-Japanese movement. These shops have suspended their
business, but such a boycott movement will not cause the S.M.C.
any worry and will be settled gradually when it is understood
that such a movement will be of no benefit to them. The
S.M.C. will adopt strict measures against anyone who intimidates
a law-abiding shop from purchasing meat from the Hongkew
District.

（手写：ll C. (Lloyd)
Information）

对牲畜短缺的无谓担忧：
中日牲畜同业公会活动活跃

一个名为“上海牲畜同业公会”的组织已由18名日本人和18名中国人组建而成。尽管苏州河南岸因生猪短缺而人心惶惶，但该公会的业务仍在推进。根据亚洲开发委员会及军方当局的指示，该公会将 regulate（监管）上海所需的牛、猪、羊、鸭等全部牲畜供应。因此，该公会将负责处理上海每年所需的72,000头牛和1,200,000头猪。该公会已在通州路购置了一块面积约18,000坪（一坪等于4平方码）的土地，用于建造牲畜围栏。当该公会成为“维新政府”的一部分后，它将向南京、汉口和上海，实际上向整个华中地区供应牲畜。

（批注：G.1）

pages.en:
MAY 1969
Shanghai

肉飢心配無要。
性畜組合軌道に乗る
—河官らの反対を漸次壓倒—

まだ元氣なことに驚かされ
人々を引っ張ロからの馬や
豚牛へのエサが不足に備
量えこその人たちだろう

い、ねじはまわらなくなつて、
腐敗。河口からの油や食料に
向つて走る貨物車團もたちゆ
くの運転からむのになつたの
たちは何らかだ。物價高騰の最
中にストライキがおき始めだ
田園の中にある町も食糧不足
で反亂ぐろのやうになつて、十日
ごろ數百頭だかの家畜がみんな
ついに半裸の狀態で道路に出
やはじめてゐる。工農組合の組
織する所のりんだといふ、塩水や
の飲み物が、大分さがつてきた
に到つてからのよそ行きのうち

た決壊から半年―今はもう雨
ごしのさみれたところばかりだ
に雨で崩れはじめた土手に近
く流れた洪水の水は、塩化か、
濁つた土色の今、周囲ゆく農
民を驚嘆と悲しみ、また絶望
させ圧縮させるほど脅かして

の被害者！チリコルカはひど
いの水に覆つたまま殘つて、数百の
成り手農家は住まひになかなかもど
れないのだ。

「どうしていいかわからない」
と言、開口は泣かんくら大粒

四月から農業省と四〇年ぶりの
夏の旱魃に悩むセノイナクやん
ぼく十人からのヨウキヤンに殺到し
たが十数家族が命を救うための
食糧を積んで、米一粒ない状態だ
そうだ。皆、米、味噌等の配給
pages.zh:
1969年5月
上海

无需担心肉类短缺。
牲畜养殖已步入正轨
——逐渐压倒河务官员等人的反对——

令人惊讶的是，尽管处境艰难，人们依然充满活力
从路口拉车的马匹
以及猪牛饲料的短缺储备
想必正是为了应对这些情况

然而，局势已陷入僵局，
腐败滋生。驶向河口运送油脂和食品的
货车车队也陷入了
停滞不前的境地，司机们不知如何是好。在物价飞涨的顶峰时期，
罢工开始爆发
乡村中的城镇也因粮食短缺
而变得如同叛乱巢穴一般，大约在十日左右，数百头家畜最终
以半裸的状态出现在道路上
开始游荡。据称由工农联盟组织
提供的盐水等
饮用水，供应已大幅减少
直至此后外来的物资中

决堤半年后——如今已是雨水
冲刷后的荒凉景象 everywhere
靠近因雨水而开始崩塌的堤岸
泛滥的洪水之水，或是盐碱化，
或是浑浊的土色，如今令周围的农民
惊叹、悲伤，又因绝望而倍感压迫与威胁

的受害者！奇里科尔卡（Chiricolca，音译）仍被严重的
洪水淹没，数百户
佃农难以返回家园。

“不知该如何是好”
说着，开口时泪如雨下，大颗泪珠

自四月以来，农业部以及饱受四十年来最严重夏季干旱困扰的塞诺伊纳克扬（Senoinakyan，音译）地区
约十名来自杨行（Yanghang，音译）的人员涌入
但仅有十几户家庭装载了用于救命的粮食，据说已处于无米下锅的状态。
所有人都在等待大米、味噌等的配给

OCT 1 4 1939

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
SECRETARY'S REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8039B/5-①
Date 18 10 39

Council Offers
Abattoir Lease
To Japanese

Public Health Dept.
Would Maintain
Control

An unidentified Japanese business group has been offered one year's lease of the Shanghai Municipal Council abattoir, it was reported by a Council official yesterday.
The official said that details of the transaction were at present being ironed out by the Japanese interests and the Municipal body. It was too early yet to reveal the sum involved in the proposed deal, he said.
The Public Health Department of the S.M.C. would continue to supervise meat inspection of the abattoir and the Council would retain its official control of the slaughterhouse, it was stated.
Offer of the lease resulted from an application made by the Japanese group in question for either a sale or rental of the property. The Council had received no reply to their proposal yesterday.

工部局向日本人
提供屠宰场租赁权

据工部局一名官员昨日称，一个身份不明的日本商业团体已获邀承租上海公共租界工部局屠宰场一年。
该官员表示，日方利益相关方正与工部局就交易细节进行磋商。他表示，目前透露拟议交易涉及的金额还为时过早。
据称，工部局公共卫生处将继续监督屠宰场的肉类检验工作，工部局也将保留对屠宰场的官方控制权。
此次租赁要约源于上述日本团体提出的购买或租赁该物业的申请。工部局至昨日尚未收到对方对该提议的回复。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
MAY 19 1939
01314

Butchers Are To Resume
Business To-day

Agree To Operate After Persuasion By Council;
Outlook Not Bright As Limited Supply Of
Pigs Available; Settlement Foreseen

As a result of persuasion from the Shanghai Municipal Council, the Chinese butchers in the Settlement have decided to resume their business to-day, according to information obtained form usually reliable sources last night.

However, the outlook for the local "pork situation" is still none too bright, it was stated, in view of the fact that the present available stocks of live hogs in the Settlement and French Concession areas amount to slightly over 2,000 head only. The daily public consumption of pigs by Shanghailanders, it was further revealed, averages around 2,000 pigs, so that unless fresh supplies are forthcoming, or unless the Chinese butchers could see their way to accepting supplies from Hongkew, no improvement in the Settlement and Concession "pork situation" could be expected in the near future.

The Chinese pork dealers in the two municipal areas are expected to resume their business to-morrow morning when the pigs which will be slaughtered by to-night will be delivered to them the following morning.

In resuming their business to-day, the Chinese butchers in the two municipal areas by no means abandon their original stand of "non-co-operation" with the live pig merchants in the Hongkew areas, it was intimated yesterday.

Settlement Seen

It is thought likely, however, that eventually the Hongkew live pigs dealers will come to terms with the Chinese butchers and pork dealers on this side of the Soochow Creek.

As pork is a daily necessity and is "perishable goods," and there being no cold storage facilities in Hongkew, the Hongkew butchers are eager to see their wares marketed the same day as the pigs are being slaughtered.

The Hongkew Chinese butchers and pork dealers have been working in close co-operation with Japanese interests, and have set up their independent guilds, while the butchers and pork dealers on this side of the Creek have their "old" guilds. The two opposing camps have been unable to see eye to eye with one another, and this had prompted the "strike" started by Settlement and Concession butchers and pork dealers last week-end.

Li Ray
Cig

《字林西报》。
1939年5月19日
01314

屠户将于今日复业

经工部局劝告后同意营业；因生猪供应有限，前景不容乐观；预计租界内将达成和解

据昨晚从通常可靠的消息来源获悉，由于上海公共租界工部局的劝告，租界内的中国屠户已决定于今日恢复营业。

然而，据悉，鉴于目前租界及法租界区域内现有的活猪库存仅略高于2,000头，当地“猪肉局势”的前景仍不太明朗。进一步透露的信息显示，上海外侨每日的猪肉平均消费量约为2,000头，因此，除非有新的供应到来，或者中国屠户能够接受来自虹口（Hongkew）的供应，否则在不久的将来，租界和法租界的“猪肉局势”难以期待有所改善。

预计两个市政区域的中国猪肉商贩将于明晨恢复营业，届时今晚屠宰的生猪将于次日清晨交付给他们。

昨日有人暗示，两个市政区域的中国屠户于今日复业，绝不意味着他们放弃原先对虹口地区活猪商人采取“不合作”的立场。

预计租界内将达成和解

然而，人们认为，苏州河此侧的中国屠户和猪肉商贩最终可能会与虹口的活猪商人达成协议。

由于猪肉是日常必需品，且属于“易腐货物”，而虹口没有冷藏设施，虹口的屠户急于在生猪屠宰当天就将货物售出。

虹口的中国屠户和猪肉商贩一直与日本势力密切合作，并建立了独立的行会，而苏州河此侧的屠户和猪肉商贩则拥有其“旧”行会。这两大对立阵营一直无法达成共识，这也促使了上周末租界和法租界屠户及猪肉商贩发起的“罢工”。

Li Ray
Cig

Shanghai Goes
Porkless As
Supply Drops

Increasing Demand For

Is Noted

Approximately 800 meat dealers
in Shanghai were forced to tell

Interviewed by Chinese newsmen,

settlement to the "whole mess".

A limited supply of the meat at
soaring prices was still to be
obtained at a number of shops.
About 1,500 shops were still selling
their left-over stock.

Owners of the latter establish-
ments were unanimous in telling
buyers that unless some settlement
is immediately reached between the
Japanese-sponsored "Cattle Market"
in Hongkew and the local slaughter
houses, there will not be an ounce
of pork by tomorrow.

Sea Food In Demand

A corresponding increase in the
demand for sea food, fowls and
vegetables was reported to have
been noted yesterday as the supply
of pork rapidly ran short.

Poultry dealers, however, were
not too optimistic about the future,
according to Chinese reports, in
view of the fact that Japanese
authorities are attempting to apply
the same law on fowl as on hogs.

During the past month, it is re-

occupied areas, were working for
the imposition of special levies on
every head of fowl brought into
the foreign-controlled areas. At
one time, a large shipment of
chicken and ducks was detained at
the North Station for non-payment
of levies.

Fish, likewise, has not escaped
the attention of the Japanese and
the Chinese puppet officials in
Shanghai, a fish market having
been set up to effect a monopoly
of the sea food trade in the entire
Shanghai area.

Fearful Of Future

Local dealers have expressed the
belief that if the pork situation is
not settled to the satisfaction of
the traders here, then the Japanese
and their puppet agents would
intensify their monopolistic mea-
sures in the fowl and sea food
businesses.

Terms dictated to the local pig
hongs by the "Cattle Market" are
that the pigs be transported here
by Japanese ships and that a tax
of $2 be paid by each pig.

"In order to fit in with the
war-time situation," it was stated,
"transportation of live stock to
Shanghai must be monopolized by
one hong."

slaughtering of pigs in the foreign-
controlled areas, two in the Set-
tlement and one in the conces-
sion. Altogether they killed ap-
proximately 7,000 heads of the cat-

《大美晚报》。1939年5月15日

随着供应下降
上海陷入无猪肉可买境地

家禽、海鲜需求
激增现象受到关注

昨日，由于公共租界和法租界的屠宰场完全关闭，上海大约800家肉商被迫告知顾客，他们的猪肉已售罄。

在接受中国记者采访时，肉商们表示希望外国控制区的当局能代表他们进行干预，以便为这“一团乱麻”带来一个令人满意的解决方案。

在一些商店里，仍能以飞涨的价格买到限量供应的猪肉。大约有1,500家商店仍在出售其库存余货。

这些店铺的店主一致告诉买家，除非虹口由日本人支持的“牛市场”与当地屠宰场之间立即达成某种协议，否则明天将连一盎司猪肉都买不到。

海鲜需求旺盛

据报道，随着猪肉供应迅速短缺，昨日对海鲜、家禽和蔬菜的需求相应增加。

然而，据中文报道，家禽经销商对未来并不太乐观，鉴于日本当局正试图将对猪实施的同样法规应用于家禽。

回顾过去一个月，占领区内的亲日经销商一直在努力对进入外国控制区的每一只家禽征收特别捐税。曾有一大批鸡鸭因未缴纳捐税而在北站被扣留。

鱼类同样未能逃脱在上海的日本人和中国伪官员的注意，一个鱼市已经建立，旨在垄断整个上海地区的海鲜贸易。

担忧未来

当地经销商认为，如果猪肉问题不能令这里的商人满意地得到解决，那么日本人及其傀儡代理人将加强在家禽和海鲜业务上的垄断措施。

“牛市场”向本地猪行强加的条件是：生猪必须由日本船只运至此处，且每头猪需缴纳2美元税款。

声明称：“为了适应战时局势，活畜运往上海必须由一家商行垄断。”

在外国控制区有三家商行从事生猪屠宰业务，其中两家在公共租界，一家在法租界。它们总共屠宰了大约7,000头牲

08074
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
MAY 1 5 1939

Pork Dealers Hold
"Go-Slow" Strike
Refuse to Co-operate With
New Hongkew Market; 2,000
Shops Affected

There will be no pork for sale in
more than 2,000 pork shops in
Shanghai to-day because the owners
have been forced to declare a "go-
slow" strike owing to the fact that
dealers have stopped buying pigs
from the interior, refusing to co-
operate and register with the new
Shanghai Cattle Market in Hongkew
which is monopolizing the pig trans-
portation business.
Many shipments of pigs bought by
the recalcitrant pig dealers have
been detained by the new market
authorities as the latter have refused
to participate in the market. As a
result of the detention many pigs
are reported to have died and the
loss will be a knotty problem to be
solved by all parties concerned in-
cluding the farmers breeding pigs
in the interior.
The authorities of the foreign
settlements have been requested to
offer assistance in settling the dead-
locked question and the strike will
be called in the hope that the au-
thorities concerned will intervene so
that a workable compromise plan
will be evolved.
The Settlement authorities have,
therefore, been called upon to solve
another important semi-political
question which is affecting the
general public. The pig dealers are
divided into two camps and while
some of them have no doubt parti-
cipated in the Japanese-sponsored
cattle market, most of them who
operate south of the creek have
adopted a non-conciliatory attitude
and stood so firm that they do not
care to sacrifice their business.
pages.zh:
08074
《字林西报》。
1939年5月15日

猪肉商举行
“怠工”罢工
拒绝与新虹口市场合作；
受影响店铺达2,000家

今日，上海两千多家猪肉铺将无猪肉出售，因为店主们被迫宣布实行“怠工”罢工。这是由于商贩们已停止从内地购买生猪，拒绝配合并在垄断生猪运输业务的新上海牲畜市场（位于虹口）进行注册。

许多由拒不合作的猪贩购买的生猪装运已被新市场当局扣留，因为这些猪贩拒绝参与该市场的运作。据报道，由于被扣留，许多生猪已经死亡，由此造成的损失将成为一个棘手的问题，需由包括内地养猪农户在内的所有相关方共同解决。

各方已请求租界当局协助解决这一僵持不下的问题，发起此次罢工是希望有关当局能够介入，从而制定出一个可行的妥协方案。

因此，租界当局被要求解决另一个影响公众的重要半政治性问题。猪肉商分为两派，其中一些人无疑参与了由日本人支持的牲畜市场，但大多数在苏州河以南经营的商人则采取了不妥协的态度，立场坚定，不愿牺牲自己的生意。

May 17, 1939.
NANLICHI
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. P. REGISTRY
No. S. D. D.

UNOFFICIAL ACTIVITY OVER SHORTAGE OF LIVESTOCK;
SINO-JAPANESE LIVESTOCK GUILD ACTIVE

A livestock guild known as the
Shanghai Livestock Guild has been formed by 18 Japanese and 18
Chinese. The business of the guild is making progress
notwithstanding the excitement on the south side of the creek
over a shortage of pigs. Acting on instructions from the
Asia Development Board and the Military authorities, the
guild will regulate the entire supply of livestock such as
cows, pigs, goats, ducks etc for Shanghai. Thus the guild
will handle the 72,000 cows and 1,200,000 pigs which are required
by Shanghai every year. The guild has already purchased a
piece of land measuring about 18,000 tsubo( one tsubo equals
to 4 square yards) on Tungchow Road for the erection of a
stockyard. When the guild has become a part of the
"Reformed Government" it will supply livestock to Nanking,
Hankow and Shanghai, in fact , to the whole of Central China.

FILE
P. A. to D. C. (Sp. Br.)

A movement to boycott the Shanghai
Livestock Guild is reported to have been started by about 2,000
Chinese shops on the south side of the creek. This is an
anti-Japanese movement. These shops have suspended their
business, but such a boycott movement will not cause the S.M.C.
any worry and will be settled gradually when it is understood
that such a movement will be of no benefit to them. The
S.M.C. will adopt strict measures against anyone who intimidates
a law-abiding shop from purchasing meat from the Hongkew
District.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 18 MAY 1939）

Commr. of Police.

关于牲畜短缺的非官方活动；
中日牲畜同业公会活跃

一个名为“上海牲畜同业公会”的组织已由18名日本人和18名中国人组建而成。尽管苏州河以南地区因生猪短缺而引发骚动，但该公会的业务仍在推进中。根据亚洲开发委员会及军方当局的指示，该公会将监管上海所需的牛、猪、羊、鸭等全部牲畜供应。因此，该公会将负责处理上海每年所需的72,000头牛和1,200,000头猪。该公会已在通州路购买了一块面积约18,000坪（一坪等于4平方码）的土地，用于建造牲畜围栏。当该公会成为“维新政府”的一部分后，它将向南京、汉口和上海，实际上向整个华中地区供应牲畜。

档案
警察局长致特别处处长（特别分部）

据报，苏州河以南地区约有2,000家中国商铺发起了一场抵制上海牲畜同业公会的运动。这是一场反日运动。这些商铺已暂停营业，但此类抵制运动不会引起工部局的任何担忧，一旦人们明白此类运动对他们毫无益处，事态将逐渐平息。工部局将对任何恐吓守法商铺从虹口区购买肉类的行为采取严厉措施。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1939年5月18日）

To Ying Yeh Pao (17/7) :-

LIVESTOCK MARKET IN HONGKEW CRIPPLED WITH DEBTS

The Livestock Market in Hongkow was established
by Mr. Matsuyen of the Bureau of Liaison of the Central
China Committee of the Asia Development Company with the
co-operation of Yang Tso-ching, Wang Kuo-yen and others.
It has a capital of $500,000.
To prevent foreigners from importing pigs
into the Foreign Settlements, the Market detailed men to
various ports in Kompo to register the pigs imported into
Shanghai. As local pork dealers refuse to buy their
meat from the Livestock Market, the daily sales of pigs
have dropped from 3,000 to 800.
We understand that the market owes a sum of
$700,000 to certain pork dealers.

致《英业报》（7月17日）：

虹口牲畜市场因债务陷入困境

虹口牲畜市场由亚细亚开发公司华中委员会联络局的松延（Matsuyen，音译）先生，在杨佐卿、王国仁等人合作下建立。其资本为50万元。

为防止外国人将猪只输入公共租界，该市场派遣人员前往宁波各港口，对输入上海的猪只进行登记。由于本地猪肉商拒绝从该牲畜市场购买肉类，猪的日销量已从3,000头降至800头。

据悉，该市场欠某些猪肉商款项达70万元。
